1.1: BOOK I HAPPY IS the man that has not walked in the counsel of the wicked, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the seat of the scornful.
1.2: But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in His law does he meditate day and night.
1.3: And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water, that brings forth its fruit in its season, and whose leaf does not wither; and in whatever he does he shall prosper.
1.4: Not so the wicked; but they are like the chaff which the wind drives away.
1.5: Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.
1.6: For the LORD regards the way of the righteous; but the way of the wicked shall perish.

2.1: Why are the nations in an uproar? And why do the peoples mutter in vain?
2.2: The kings of the earth stand up, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against His anointed:
2.3: 'Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.'
2.4: He that sits in heaven laughs, the Lord has them in derision.
2.5: Then will He speak to them in His wrath, and affright them in His sore displeasure:
2.6: 'Truly it is I that have established My king upon Zion, My holy mountain.'
2.7: I will tell of the decree: the LORD said to me: 'You are My son, this day have I begotten you.
2.8: Ask of Me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession.
2.9: You shall break them with a rod of iron; you shall dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.'
2.10: Now therefore, O you kings, be wise; be admonished, you judges of the earth.
2.11: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
2.12: Do homage in purity, lest He be angry, and you perish in the way, when suddenly His wrath is kindled. Happy are all they that take refuge in Him.

3.1: (3-1) A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son. (3-2) LORD, how many are my adversaries become! Many are they that rise up against me.
3.2: (3-3) Many there are that say of my soul: 'There is no salvation for him in God.' Selah
3.3: (3-4) But you, O LORD, are a shield about me; my glory, and the lifter up of my head.
3.4: (3-5) With my voice I call to the LORD, and He answers me out of His holy mountain. Selah
3.5: (3-6) I lay me down, and I sleep; I awake, for the LORD sustains me.
3.6: (3-7) I am not afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about.
3.7: (3-8) Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God; for You have smitten all my enemies upon the cheek, You have broken the teeth of the wicked.
3.8: (3-9) Salvation belongs to the LORD; Your blessing be upon Your people. Selah

4.1: (4-1) For the Leader; with string-music. A Psalm of David. (4-2) Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness, You who did set me free when I was in distress; be gracious to me, and hear my prayer.
4.2: (4-3) O you sons of men, how long shall my glory be put to shame, in that you love vanity, and seek after falsehood? Selah
4.3: (4-4) But know that the LORD has set apart the godly man as His own; the LORD will hear when I call to Him.
4.4: (4-5) Tremble, and sin not; commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah
4.5: (4-6) Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the LORD.
4.6: (4-7) Many there are that say: 'Oh that we could see some good!' LORD, lift You up the light of Your countenance upon us.
4.7: (4-8) You have put gladness in my heart, more than when their corn and their wine increase.
4.8: (4-9) In peace will I both lay me down and sleep; for You, LORD, make me dwell alone in safety.

5.1: (5-1) For the Leader; upon the Nehiloth. A Psalm of David. (5-2) Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.
5.2: (5-3) Hearken to the voice of my cry, my King, and my God; for to You do I pray.
5.3: (5-4) O LORD, in the morning shall You hear my voice; in the morning will I order my prayer to You, and will look forward.
5.4: (5-5) For You are not a God that has pleasure in wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You.
5.5: (5-6) The boasters shall not stand in Your sight; You hate all workers of iniquity.
5.6: (5-7) You destroy them that speak falsehood; the LORD abhors the man of blood and of deceit.
5.7: (5-8) But as for me, in the abundance of Your lovingkindness will I come into Your house; I will bow down toward Your holy temple in the fear of You.
5.8: (5-9) O LORD, lead me in Your righteousness because of them that lie in wait for me; make Your way straight before my face.
5.9: (5-10) For there is no sincerity in their mouth; their inward part is a yawning gulf, their throat is an open sepulchre; they make smooth their tongue.
5.10: (5-11) Hold them guilty, O God, let them fall by their own counsels; cast them down in the multitude of their transgressions; for they have rebelled against You.
5.11: (5-12) So shall all those that take refuge in You rejoice, they shall ever shout for joy, and You shall shelter them; let them also that love Your name exult in You.
5.12: (5-13) For You do bless the righteous; O LORD, You do encompass him with favour as with a shield.

6.1: (6-1) For the Leader; with string-music; on the Sheminith. A Psalm of David. (6-2) O LORD, rebuke me not in Your anger, neither chasten me in Your wrath.
6.2: (6-3) Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I languish away; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are affrighted.
6.3: (6-4) My soul also is sore affrighted; and You, O LORD, how long?
6.4: (6-5) Return, O LORD, deliver my soul; save me for Your mercy's sake.
6.5: (6-6) For in death there is no remembrance of You; in the nether-world who will give You thanks?
6.6: (6-7) I am weary with my groaning; every night make I my bed to swim; I melt away my couch with my tears.
6.7: (6-8) My eye is dimmed because of vexation; it waxes old because of all my adversaries.
6.8: (6-9) Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity; for the LORD has heard the voice of my weeping.
6.9: (6-10) The LORD has heard my supplication; the LORD receives my prayer.
6.10: (6-11) All my enemies shall be ashamed and sore affrighted; they shall turn back, they shall be ashamed suddenly.

7.1: (7-1) Shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD, concerning Cush a Benjamite. (7-2) O LORD my God, in You have I taken refuge; save me from all them that pursue me, and deliver me;
7.2: (7-3) Lest he tear my soul like a lion, rending it in pieces, while there is none to deliver.
7.3: (7-4) O LORD my God, if I have done this; if there be iniquity in my hands;
7.4: (7-5) If I have requited him that did evil to me, or spoiled my adversary to emptiness;
7.5: (7-6) Let the enemy pursue my soul, and overtake it, and tread my life down to the earth; yes, let him lay my glory in the dust. Selah
7.6: (7-7) Arise, O LORD, in Your anger, lift up Yourself in indignation against my adversaries; yes, awake for me at the judgment which You have commanded.
7.7: (7-8) And let the congregation of the peoples compass You about, and over them return You on high.
7.8: (7-9) O LORD, who minister judgment to the peoples, judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to my integrity that is in me.
7.9: (7-10) Oh that a full measure of evil might come upon the wicked, and that You would establish the righteous; for the righteous God tries the heart and reins.
7.10: (7-11) My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
7.11: (7-12) God is a righteous judge, yes, a God that has indignation every day:
7.12: (7-13) If a man turn not, He will whet His sword, He has bent His bow, and made it ready;
7.13: (7-14) He has also prepared for him the weapons of death, yes, His arrows which He made sharp.
7.14: (7-15) Behold, he travails with iniquity; yes, he conceives mischief, and brings forth falsehood.
7.15: (7-16) He has digged a pit, and hollowed it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.
7.16: (7-17) His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violence shall come down upon his own pate.
7.17: (7-18) I will give thanks to the LORD according to His righteousness; and will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

8.1: (8-1) For the Leader; upon the Gittith. A Psalm of David. (8-2) O LORD, our Lord, how glorious is Your name in all the earth! whose majesty is rehearsed above the heavens.
8.2: (8-3) Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings have You founded strength, because of Your adversaries; that You might still the enemy and the avenger.
8.3: (8-4) When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have established;
8.4: (8-5) What is man, that You are mindful of him? and the son of man, that You think of him?
8.5: (8-6) Yet You have made him but little lower than the angels, and have crowned him with glory and honour.
8.6: (8-7) You have made him to have dominion over the works of Your hands; You have put all things under His feet:
8.7: (8-8) Sheep and oxen, all of them, yes, and the beasts of the field;
8.8: (8-9) The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea; whatever passes through the paths of the seas.
8.9: (8-10) O LORD, our Lord, how glorious is Your name in all the earth!

9.1: (9-1) For the Leader; upon Muthlabben. A Psalm of David. (9-2) I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart; I will tell of all Your marvellous works.
9.2: (9-3) I will be glad and exult in You; I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High:
9.3: (9-4) When my enemies are turned back, they stumble and perish at Your presence;
9.4: (9-5) For You have maintained my right and my cause; You sat upon the throne as the righteous Judge.
9.5: (9-6) You have rebuked the nations, You have destroyed the wicked, You have blotted out their name for ever and ever.
9.6: (9-7) O you enemy, the waste places are come to an end for ever; and the cities which you did uproot, their very memorial is perished.
9.7: (9-8) But the LORD is enthroned for ever; He has established His throne for judgment.
9.8: (9-9) And He will judge the world in righteousness, He will minister judgment to the peoples with equity.
9.9: (9-10) The LORD also will be a high tower for the oppressed, a high tower in times of trouble;
9.10: (9-11) And they that know Your name will put their trust in You; for you, LORD, have not forsaken them that seek You.
9.11: (9-12) Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; declare among the peoples His doings.
9.12: (9-13) For He that avenges blood has remembered them; He has not forgotten the cry of the humble.
9.13: (9-14) Be gracious to me, O LORD, behold my affliction at the hands of them that hate me; You that lifts me up from the gates of death;
9.14: (9-15) That I may tell of all Your praise in the gates of the daughter of Zion, that I may rejoice in Your salvation.
9.15: (9-16) The nations are sunk down in the pit that they made; in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.
9.16: (9-17) The LORD has made Himself known, He has executed judgment, the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah
9.17: (9-18) The wicked shall return to the nether-world, even all the nations that forget God.
9.18: (9-19) For the needy shall not alway be forgotten, nor the expectation of the poor perish for ever.
9.19: (9-20) Arise, O LORD, let not man prevail; let the nations be judged in Your sight.
9.20: (9-21) Set terror over them, O LORD; let the nations know they are but men. Selah

10.1: Why stand You afar off, O LORD? Why hide You Yourself in times of trouble?
10.2: Through the pride of the wicked the poor is hotly pursued, they are taken in the devices that they have imagined.
10.3: For the wicked boasts of his heart's desire, and the covetous vaunts himself, though he contemn the LORD.
10.4: The wicked, in the pride of his countenance, says: 'He will not require'; all his thoughts are: 'There is no God.'
10.5: His ways prosper at all times; Your judgments are far above out of his sight; as for all his adversaries, he puffs at them.
10.6: He says in his heart: 'I shall not be moved, I who to all generations shall not be in adversity.'
10.7: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue is mischief and iniquity.
10.8: He sits in the lurking-places of the villages; in secret places does he slay the innocent; his eyes are on the watch for the helpless.
10.9: He lies in wait in a secret place as a lion in his lair, he lies in wait to catch the poor; he does catch the poor, when he draws him up in his net.
10.10: He crouches, he bows down, and the helpless fall into his mighty claws.
10.11: He has said in his heart: 'God has forgotten; He hides His face; He will never see.'
10.12: Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up Your hand; forget not the humble.
10.13: Wherefore does the wicked contemn God, and say in his heart: 'You will not require'?
10.14: You have seen; for You behold trouble and vexation, to requite them with Your hand; to You the helpless commits himself; You have been the helper of the fatherless.
10.15: Break You the arm of the wicked; and as for the evil man, search out his wickedness, till none be found.
10.16: The LORD is King for ever and ever; the nations are perished out of His land.
10.17: LORD, You have heard the desire of the humble: You will direct their heart, You will cause Your ear to attend;
10.18: To right the fatherless and the oppressed, that man who is of the earth may be terrible no more.

11.1: For the Leader. A Psalm of David. In the LORD have I taken refuge; how say you to my soul: 'Flee you! to your mountain, you birds'?
11.2: For, indeed, the wicked bend the bow, they have made ready their arrow upon the string, that they may shoot in darkness at the upright in heart.
11.3: When the foundations are destroyed, what has the righteous worked?
11.4: The LORD is in His holy temple, the LORD, His throne is in heaven; His eyes behold, His eyelids try, the children of men.
11.5: The LORD tries the righteous; but the wicked and him that loves violence His soul hates.
11.6: Upon the wicked He will cause to rain coals; fire and brimstone and burning wind shall be the portion of their cup.
11.7: For the LORD is righteous, He loves righteousness; the upright shall behold His face.

12.1: (12-1) For the Leader; on the Sheminith. A Psalm of David. (12-2) Help, LORD; for the godly man ceases; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.
12.2: (12-3) They speak falsehood every one with his neighbour; with flattering lip, and with a double heart, do they speak.
12.3: (12-4) May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that speaks proud things!
12.4: (12-5) Who have said: 'Our tongue will we make mighty; our lips are with us: who is lord over us?'
12.5: (12-6) 'For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise', says the LORD; 'I will set him in safety at whom they puff.'
12.6: (12-7) The words of the LORD are pure words, as silver tried in a crucible on the earth, refined seven times.
12.7: (12-8) You will keep them, O LORD; You will preserve us from this generation for ever.
12.8: (12-9) The wicked walk on every side, when vileness is exalted among the sons of men.

13.1: (13-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (13-2) How long, O LORD, will You forget me for ever? How long will You hide Your face from me?
13.2: (13-3) How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart by day? How long shall my enemy be exalted over me?
13.3: (13-4) Behold You, and answer me, O LORD my God; lighten my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death;
13.4: (13-5) Lest my enemy say: 'I have prevailed against him'; lest my adversaries rejoice when I am moved.
13.5: (13-6) But as for me, in Your mercy do I trust; my heart shall rejoice in Your salvation.
13.6: (13-6) I will sing to the LORD, because He has dealt bountifully with me.

14.1: For the Leader. A Psalm of David. The fool has said in his heart: 'There is no God'; they have dealt corruptly, they have done abominably; there is none that does good.
14.2: The LORD looked forth from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any man of understanding, that did seek after God.
14.3: They are all corrupt, they are together become impure; there is none that does good, no, not one.
14.4: 'Shall not all the workers of iniquity know it, who eat up My people as they eat bread, and call not upon the LORD?'
14.5: There are they in great fear; for God is with the righteous generation.
14.6: You would put to shame the counsel of the poor, but the LORD is his refuge.
14.7: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When the LORD turns the captivity of His people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

15.1: A Psalm of David. LORD, who shall sojourn in Your tabernacle? Who shall dwell upon Your holy mountain?
15.2: He that walks uprightly, and works righteousness, and speaks truth in his heart;
15.3: That has no slander upon his tongue, nor does evil to his fellow, nor takes up a reproach against his neighbour;
15.4: In whose eyes a vile person is despised, but he honours them that fear the LORD; he that swears to his own hurt, and changes not;
15.5: He that puts not out his money on interest, nor takes a bribe against the innocent. He that does these things shall never be moved.

16.1: Michtam of David. Keep me, O God; for I have taken refuge in You.
16.2: I have said to the LORD: 'You are my Lord; I have no good but in You';
16.3: As for the holy that are in the earth, they are the excellent in whom is all my delight.
16.4: Let the idols of them be multiplied that make suit to another; their drink-offerings of blood will I not offer, nor take their names upon my lips.
16.5: O LORD, the portion of my inheritance and of my cup, You maintain my lot.
16.6: The lines are fallen to me in pleasant places; yes, I have a goodly heritage.
16.7: I will bless the LORD, who has given me counsel; yes, in the night seasons my reins instruct me.
16.8: I have set the LORD always before me; surely He is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
16.9: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoices; my flesh also dwells in safety;
16.10: For You will not abandon my soul to the nether-world; neither will You suffer Your godly one to see the pit.
16.11: You make me to know the path of life; in Your presence is fulness of joy, in Your right hand bliss for evermore.

17.1: A Prayer of David. Hear the right, O LORD, attend to my cry; give ear to my prayer from lips without deceit.
17.2: Let my judgment come forth from Your presence; let Your eyes behold equity.
17.3: You have tried my heart, You have visited it in the night; You have tested me, and You find not that I had a thought which should not pass my mouth.
17.4: As for the doings of men, by the word of Your lips I have kept me from the ways of the violent.
17.5: My steps have held fast to Your paths, my feet have not slipped.
17.6: As for me, I call upon You, for You will answer me, O God; incline Your ear to me, hear my speech.
17.7: Make passing great Your mercies, O You that saves by Your right hand from assailants them that take refuge in You.
17.8: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me in the shadow of Your wings,
17.9: From the wicked that oppress, my deadly enemies, that compass me about.
17.10: Their gross heart they have shut tight, with their mouth they speak proudly.
17.11: At our every step they have now encompassed us; they set their eyes to cast us down to the earth.
17.12: He is like a lion that is eager to tear in pieces, and like a young lion lurking in secret places.
17.13: Arise, O LORD, confront him, cast him down; deliver my soul from the wicked, by Your sword;
17.14: From men, by Your hand, O LORD, from men of the world, whose portion is in this life, and whose belly You fill with Your treasure; who have children in plenty, and leave their abundance to their babes.
17.15: As for me, I shall behold Your face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with Your likeness.

18.1: (18-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David the servant of the LORD, who spoke to the LORD the words of this song in the day that the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul; (18-2) And he said: I love you, O LORD, my strength.
18.2: (18-3) The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in Him I take refuge; my shield, and my horn of salvation, my high tower.
18.3: (18-4) Praised, I cry, is the LORD, and I am saved from my enemies.
18.4: (18-5) The cords of Death compassed me, and the floods of Belial assailed me.
18.5: (18-6) The cords of Sheol surrounded me; the snares of Death confronted me.
18.6: (18-7) In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried to my God; out of His temple He heard my voice, and my cry came before Him to His ears.
18.7: (18-8) Then the earth did shake and quake, the foundations also of the mountains did tremble; they were shaken, because He was wroth.
18.8: (18-9) Smoke arose up in His nostrils, and fire out of His mouth did devour; coals flamed forth from Him.
18.9: (18-10) He bowed the heavens also, and came down; and thick darkness was under His feet.
18.10: (18-11) And He rode upon a cherub, and did fly; yes, He did swoop down upon the wings of the wind.
18.11: (18-12) He made darkness His hiding-place, His pavilion round about Him; darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
18.12: (18-13) At the brightness before Him, there passed through His thick clouds hailstones and coals of fire.
18.13: (18-14) The LORD also thundered in the heavens, and the Most High gave forth His voice; hailstones and coals of fire.
18.14: (18-15) And He sent out His arrows, and scattered them; and He shot forth lightnings, and discomfited them.
18.15: (18-16) And the channels of waters appeared, and the foundations of the world were laid bare, at Your rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of Your nostrils.
18.16: (18-17) He sent from on high, He took me; He drew me out of many waters.
18.17: (18-18) He delivered me from my enemy most strong, and from them that hated me, for they were too mighty for me.
18.18: (18-19) They confronted me in the day of my calamity; but the LORD was a stay to me.
18.19: (18-20) He brought me forth also into a large place; He delivered me, because He delighted in me.
18.20: (18-21) The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands has He recompensed me.
18.21: (18-22) For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
18.22: (18-23) For all His ordinances were before me, and I put not away His statutes from me.
18.23: (18-24) And I was single-hearted with Him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.
18.24: (18-25) Therefore has the LORD recompensed me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in His eyes.
18.25: (18-26) With the merciful You do show Yourself merciful, with the upright man You do show Yourself upright;
18.26: (18-27) With the pure You do show Yourself pure; and with the crooked You do show Yourself subtle.
18.27: (18-28) For You do save the afflicted people; but the haughty eyes You do humble.
18.28: (18-29) For You do light my lamp; the LORD my God does lighten my darkness.
18.29: (18-30) For by You I run upon a troop; and by my God do I scale a wall.
18.30: (18-31) As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD is tried; He is a shield to all them that take refuge in Him.
18.31: (18-32) For who is God, save the LORD? And who is a Rock, except our God?
18.32: (18-33) The God that girds me with strength, and makes my way straight;
18.33: (18-34) Who makes my feet like hinds', and sets me upon my high places;
18.34: (18-35) Who trains my hands for war, so that my arms do bend a bow of brass.
18.35: (18-36) You have also given me Your shield of salvation, and Your right hand has holden me up; and Your condescension has made me great.
18.36: (18-37) You have enlarged my steps under me, and my feet have not slipped.
18.37: (18-38) I have pursued my enemies, and overtaken them; neither did I turn back till they were consumed.
18.38: (18-39) I have smitten them through, so that they are not able to rise; they are fallen under my feet.
18.39: (18-40) For You have girded me with strength to the battle; You have subdued under me those that rose up against me.
18.40: (18-41) You have also made my enemies turn their backs to me, and I did cut off them that hate me.
18.41: (18-42) They cried, but there was none to save; even to the LORD, but He answered them not.
18.42: (18-43) Then did I beat them small as the dust before the wind; I did cast them out as the mire of the streets.
18.43: (18-44) You have delivered me from the contentions of the people; You have made me the head of the nations; a people whom I have not known serve me.
18.44: (18-45) As soon as they hear of me, they obey me; the sons of the stranger dwindle away before me.
18.45: (18-46) The sons of the stranger fade away, and come trembling out of their close places.
18.46: (18-47) The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock; and exalted be the God of my salvation;
18.47: (18-48) Even the God that executes vengeance for me, and subdues peoples under me.
18.48: (18-49) He delivers me from my enemies; yes, You lift me up above them that rise up against me; You deliver me from the violent man.
18.49: (18-50) Therefore I will give thanks to You, O LORD, among the nations, and will sing praises to Your name.
18.50: (18-51) Great salvation gives He to His king; and shows mercy to His anointed, to David and to his seed, for evermore.

19.1: (19-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (19-2) The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament shows His handiwork;
19.2: (19-3) Day to day utters speech, and night to night reveals knowledge;
19.3: (19-4) There is no speech, there are no words, neither is their voice heard.
19.4: (19-5) Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In them has He set a tent for the sun,
19.5: (19-6) Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoices as a strong man to run his course.
19.6: (19-7) His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit to the ends of it; and there is nothing hid from the heat of it.
19.7: (19-8) The law of the LORD is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.
19.8: (19-9) The precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes.
19.9: (19-10) The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring for ever; the ordinances of the LORD are true, they are righteous altogether;
19.10: (19-11) More to be desired are they than gold, yes, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.
19.11: (19-12) Moreover by them is Your servant warned; in keeping of them there is great reward.
19.12: (19-13) Who can discern his errors? Clear You me from hidden faults.
19.13: (19-14) Keep back Your servant also from presumptuous sins, that they may not have dominion over me; then shall I be faultless, and I shall be clear from great transgression.
19.14: (19-15) Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.

20.1: (20-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (20-2) The LORD answer you in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob set you up on high;
20.2: (20-3) Send forth your help from the sanctuary, and support you out of Zion;
20.3: (20-4) Receive the memorial of all your meal-offerings, and accept the fat of your burnt-sacrifice; Selah
20.4: (20-5) Grant you according to your own heart, and fulfil all your counsel.
20.5: (20-6) We will shout for joy in your victory, and in the name of our God we will set up our standards; the LORD fulfil all your petitions.
20.6: (20-7) Now know I that the LORD saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven with the mighty acts of His saving right hand.
20.7: (20-8) Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; but we will make mention of the name of the LORD our God.
20.8: (20-9) They are bowed down and fallen; but we are risen, and stand upright.
20.9: (20-10) Save, LORD; let the King answer us in the day that we call.

21.1: (21-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (21-2) O LORD, in Your strength the king rejoices; and in Your salvation how greatly does he exult!
21.2: (21-3) You have given him his heart's desire, and the request of his lips You have not withholden. Selah
21.3: (21-4) For You meet him with choice blessings; You set a crown of fine gold on his head.
21.4: (21-5) He asked life of You, You gave it him; even length of days for ever and ever.
21.5: (21-6) His glory is great through Your salvation; honour and majesty do You lay upon him.
21.6: (21-7) For You make him most blessed for ever; You make him glad with joy in Your presence.
21.7: (21-8) For the king trusts in the LORD, yes, in the mercy of the Most High; he shall not be moved.
21.8: (21-9) Your hand shall be equal to all your enemies; your right hand shall overtake those that hate you.
21.9: (21-10) You shall make them as a fiery furnace in the time of your anger; the LORD shall swallow them up in His wrath, and the fire shall devour them.
21.10: (21-11) Their fruit will you destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.
21.11: (21-12) For they intended evil against you, they imagined a device, with which they shall not prevail.
21.12: (21-13) For you shall make them turn their back, you shall make ready with your bowstrings against the face of them.
21.13: (21-14) Be You exalted, O LORD, in Your strength; so will we sing and praise Your power.

22.1: (22-1) For the Leader; upon Aijeleth ha-Shahar. A Psalm of David. (22-2) My God, my God, why have You forsaken me, and are far from my help at the words of my cry?
22.2: (22-3) O my God, I call by day, but You answer not; and at night, and there is no surcease for me.
22.3: (22-4) Yet You are holy, O You that are enthroned upon the praises of Israel.
22.4: (22-5) In You did our fathers trust; they trusted, and You did deliver them.
22.5: (22-6) To You they cried, and escaped; in You did they trust, and were not ashamed.
22.6: (22-7) But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people.
22.7: (22-8) All they that see me laugh me to scorn; they shoot out the lip, they shake the head:
22.8: (22-9) 'Let him commit himself to the LORD! let Him rescue him; let Him deliver him, seeing He delights in him.'
22.9: (22-10) For You are He that took me out of the womb; You made me trust when I was upon my mother's breasts.
22.10: (22-11) Upon You I have been cast from my birth; You are my God from my mother's womb.
22.11: (22-12) Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help.
22.12: (22-13) Many bulls have encompassed me; strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.
22.13: (22-14) They open wide their mouth against me, as a ravening and a roaring lion.
22.14: (22-15) I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint; my heart is become like wax; it is melted in my inmost parts.
22.15: (22-16) My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaves to my throat; and You lay me in the dust of death.
22.16: (22-17) For dogs have encompassed me; a company of evil-doers have inclosed me; like a lion, they are at my hands and my feet.
22.17: (22-18) I may count all my bones; they look and gloat over me.
22.18: (22-19) They part my garments among them, and for my vesture do they cast lots.
22.19: (22-20) But You, O LORD, be not far off; O You my strength, hasten to help me.
22.20: (22-21) Deliver my soul from the sword; my only one from the power of the dog.
22.21: (22-22) Save me from the lion's mouth; yes, from the horns of the wild-oxen do You answer me.
22.22: (22-23) I will declare Your name to my brethren; in the midst of the congregation will I praise You.
22.23: (22-24) 'You that fear the LORD, praise Him; all you the seed of Jacob, glorify Him; and stand in awe of Him, all you the seed of Israel.
22.24: (22-25) For He has not despised nor abhorred the lowliness of the poor; neither has He hid His face from him; but when he cried to Him, He heard.'
22.25: (22-26) From You comes my praise in the great congregation; I will pay my vows before them that fear Him.
22.26: (22-27) Let the humble eat and be satisfied; let them praise the LORD that seek after Him; may your heart be quickened for ever!
22.27: (22-28) All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the LORD; and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before You.
22.28: (22-29) For the kingdom is the LORD'S; and He is the ruler over the nations.
22.29: (22-30) All the fat ones of the earth shall eat and worship; all they that go down to the dust shall kneel before Him, even he that cannot keep his soul alive.
22.30: (22-31) A seed shall serve him; it shall be told of the Lord to the next generation.
22.31: (22-32) They shall come and shall declare His righteousness to a people that shall be born, that He has done it.

23.1: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
23.2: He makes me to lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside the still waters.
23.3: He restores my soul; He guides me in straight paths for His name's sake.
23.4: Yes, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
23.5: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You have anointed my head with oil; my cup runs over.
23.6: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life; and I shall dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

24.1: A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD'S, and the fulness of it; the world, and they that dwell in it.
24.2: For He has founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the floods.
24.3: Who shall ascend into the mountain of the LORD? and who shall stand in His holy place?
24.4: He that has clean hands, and a pure heart; who has not taken My name in vain, and has not sworn deceitfully.
24.5: He shall receive a blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
24.6: Such is the generation of them that seek after Him, that seek Your face, even Jacob. Selah
24.7: Lift up your heads, O you gates, and be you lifted up, you everlasting doors; that the King of glory may come in.
24.8: 'Who is the King of glory?' 'The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.'
24.9: Lift up your heads, O you gates, yes, lift them up, you everlasting doors; that the King of glory may come in.
24.10: 'Who then is the King of glory?' 'The LORD of hosts; He is the King of glory.' Selah

25.1: A Psalm of David. To You, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.
25.2: O my God, in You have I trusted, let me not be ashamed; let not my enemies triumph over me.
25.3: Yes, none that wait for You shall be ashamed; they shall be ashamed that deal treacherously without cause.
25.4: Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths.
25.5: Guide me in Your truth, and teach me; for You are the God of my salvation; for You do I wait all the day.
25.6: Remember, O LORD, Your compassions and Your mercies; for they have been from of old.
25.7: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions; according to Your mercy remember You me, for Your goodness' sake, O LORD.
25.8: Good and upright is the LORD; therefore does He instruct sinners in the way.
25.9: He guides The humble in justice; and He teaches the humble His way.
25.10: All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth to such as keep His covenant and His testimonies.
25.11: For Your name's sake, O LORD, pardon my iniquity, for it is great.
25.12: What man is he that fears the LORD? him will He instruct in the way that He should choose.
25.13: His soul shall abide in prosperity; and his seed shall inherit the land.
25.14: The counsel of the LORD is with them that fear Him; and His covenant, to make them know it.
25.15: My eyes are ever toward the LORD; for He will bring forth my feet out of the net.
25.16: Turn You to me, and be gracious to me; for I am solitary and afflicted.
25.17: The troubles of my heart are enlarged; O bring You me out of my distresses.
25.18: See my affliction and my travail; and forgive all my sins.
25.19: Consider how many are my enemies, and the cruel hatred with which they hate me.
25.20: O keep my soul, and deliver me; let me not be ashamed, for I have taken refuge in You.
25.21: Let integrity and uprightness preserve me, because I wait for You.
25.22: Redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.

26.1: A Psalm of David. Judge me, O LORD, for I have walked in my integrity, and I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.
26.2: Examine me, O LORD, and try me; test my reins and my heart.
26.3: For Your mercy is before my eyes; and I have walked in Your truth.
26.4: I have not sat with men of falsehood; neither will I go in with dissemblers.
26.5: I hate the gathering of evil doers, and will not sit with the wicked.
26.6: I will wash my hands in innocency; so will I compass Your altar, O LORD,
26.7: That I may make the voice of thanksgiving to be heard, and tell of all Your wondrous works.
26.8: LORD, I love the habitation of Your house, and the place where Your glory dwells.
26.9: Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with men of blood;
26.10: In whose hands is craftiness, and their right hand is full of bribes.
26.11: But as for me, I will walk in my integrity; redeem me, and be gracious to me.
26.12: My foot stands in an even place; in the congregations will I bless the LORD.

27.1: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
27.2: When evil-doers came upon me to eat up my flesh, even my adversaries and my foes, they stumbled and fell.
27.3: Though a host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear; though war should rise up against me, even then will I be confident.
27.4: One thing have I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the graciousness of the LORD, and to visit early in His temple.
27.5: For He conceals me in His pavilion in the day of evil; He hides me in the covert of His tent; He lifts me up upon a rock.
27.6: And now shall my head be lifted up above my enemies round about me; and I will offer in His tabernacle sacrifices with trumpet-sound; I will sing, yes, I will sing praises to the LORD.
27.7: Hear, O LORD, when I call with my voice, and be gracious to me, and answer me.
27.8: In Your behalf my heart has said: 'Seek you My face'; Your face, LORD, will I seek.
27.9: Hide not Your face from me; put not Your servant away in anger; You have been my help; cast me not off, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.
27.10: For though my father and my mother have forsaken me, the LORD will take me up.
27.11: Teach me Your way, O LORD; and lead me in an even path, because of them that lie in wait for me.
27.12: Deliver me not over to the will of my adversaries; for false witnesses are risen up against me, and such as breathe out violence.
27.13: If I had not believed to look upon the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living! —
27.14: Wait on the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; yes, wait you for the LORD.

28.1: A Psalm of David. To you, O LORD, do I call; my Rock, be not You deaf to me; lest, if You be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.
28.2: Hear the voice of my supplications, when I cry to You, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy Sanctuary.
28.3: Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity; who speak peace with their neighbours, but evil is in their hearts.
28.4: Give them according to their deeds, and according to the evil of their endeavours; give them after the work of their hands; render to them their desert.
28.5: Because they give no heed to the works of the LORD, nor to the operation of His hands; He will break them down and not build them up.
28.6: Blessed be the LORD, because He has heard the voice of my supplications.
28.7: The LORD is my strength and my shield, in Him has my heart trusted, and I am helped; therefore my heart greatly rejoices, and with my song will I praise Him.
28.8: The LORD is a strength to them; and He is a stronghold of salvation to His anointed.
28.9: Save Your people, and bless Your inheritance; and tend them, and carry them for ever.

29.1: A Psalm of David. Ascribe to the LORD, O you sons of might, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
29.2: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due to His name; worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.
29.3: The voice of the LORD is upon the waters; the God of glory thunders, even the LORD upon many waters.
29.4: The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is full of majesty.
29.5: The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars; yes, the LORD breaks in pieces the cedars of Lebanon.
29.6: He makes them also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild-ox.
29.7: The voice of the LORD hews out flames of fire.
29.8: The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness; the LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
29.9: The voice of the LORD makes the hinds to calve, and strips the forests bare; and in His temple all say: 'Glory.'
29.10: The LORD sat enthroned at the flood; yes, the LORD sits as King for ever.
29.11: The LORD will give strength to His people; the LORD will bless his people with peace.

30.1: (30-1) A Psalm; a Song at the Dedication of the House; of David. (30-2) I will extol you, O LORD, for You have raised me up, and have not suffered my enemies to rejoice over me.
30.2: (30-3) O LORD my God, I cried to You, and You did heal me;
30.3: (30-4) O LORD, You brought up my soul from the nether-world; You did keep me alive, that I should not go down to the pit.
30.4: (30-5) Sing praise to the LORD, O you His godly ones, and give thanks to His holy name.
30.5: (30-6) For His anger is but for a moment, His favour is for a life-time; weeping may tarry for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
30.6: (30-7) Now I had said in my security: 'I shall never be moved.'
30.7: (30-8) You had established, O LORD, in Your favour my mountain as a stronghold — You did hide Your face; I was affrighted.
30.8: (30-9) To You, O LORD, did I call, and to the LORD I made supplication:
30.9: (30-10) 'What profit is there in my blood, when I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise You? shall it declare Your truth?
30.10: (30-11) Hear, O LORD, and be gracious to me; LORD, be You my helper.'
30.11: (30-12) You did turn for me my mourning into dancing; You did loose my sackcloth, and gird me with gladness;
30.12: (30-13) So that my glory may sing praise to You, and not be silent; O LORD my God, I will give thanks to You for ever.

31.1: (31-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (31-2) In you, O LORD, have I taken refuge; let me never be ashamed; deliver me in Your righteousness.
31.2: (31-3) Incline Your ear to me, deliver me speedily; be You to me a rock of refuge, even a fortress of defence, to save me.
31.3: (31-4) For You are my rock and my fortress; therefore for Your name's sake lead me and guide me.
31.4: (31-5) Bring me forth out of the net that they have hidden for me; for You are my stronghold.
31.5: (31-6) Into Your hand I commit my spirit; You have redeemed me, O LORD, You God of truth.
31.6: (31-7) I hate them that regard lying vanities; but I trust in the LORD.
31.7: (31-8) I will be glad and rejoice in Your lovingkindness; for You have seen my affliction, You have taken cognizance of the troubles of my soul,
31.8: (31-9) And You have not given me over into the hand of the enemy; You have set my feet in a broad place.
31.9: (31-10) Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I am in distress; my eye wastes away with vexation, yes, my soul and my body.
31.10: (31-11) For my life is spent in sorrow, and my years in sighing; my strength fails because of my iniquity, and my bones are wasted away.
31.11: (31-12) Because of all my adversaries I am become a reproach, yes, to my neighbours exceedingly, and a dread to my acquaintance; they that see me without flee from me.
31.12: (31-13) I am forgotten as a dead man out of mind; I am like a useless vessel.
31.13: (31-14) For I have heard the whispering of many, terror on every side; while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.
31.14: (31-15) But as for me, I have trusted in You, O LORD; I have said: 'You are my God.'
31.15: (31-16) My times are in Your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies, and from them that persecute me.
31.16: (31-17) Make Your face to shine upon Your servant; save me in Your lovingkindness.
31.17: (31-18) O LORD, let me not be ashamed, for I have called upon You; let the wicked be ashamed, let them be put to silence in the nether-world.
31.18: (31-19) Let the lying lips be dumb, which speak arrogantly against the righteous, with pride and contempt.
31.19: (31-20) Oh how abundant is Your goodness, which You have laid up for them that fear You; which You have worked for them that take their refuge in You, in the sight of the sons of men!
31.20: (31-21) You hide them in the covert of Your presence from the plottings of man; You conceal them in a pavilion from the strife of tongues.
31.21: (31-22) Blessed be the LORD; for He has shown me His wondrous lovingkindness in an entrenched city.
31.22: (31-23) As for me, I said in my haste: 'I am cut off from before Your eyes'; nevertheless You heard the voice of my supplications when I cried to You.
31.23: (31-24) O love the LORD, all you His godly ones; the LORD preserves the faithful, and plentifully repays him that acts haughtily.
31.24: (31-25) Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you that wait for the LORD.

32.1: A Psalm of David. Maschil. Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is pardoned.
32.2: Happy is the man to whom the LORD counts not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.
32.3: When I kept silence, my bones wore away through my groaning all the day long.
32.4: For day and night Your hand was heavy upon me; my sap was turned as in the droughts of summer. Selah
32.5: I acknowledged my sin to You, and my iniquity have I not hid; I said: 'I will make confession concerning my transgressions to the LORD' — and You, You forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah
32.6: For this let every one that is godly pray to You in a time when You may be found; surely, when the great waters overflow, they will not reach to him.
32.7: You are my hiding-place; You will preserve me from the adversary; with songs of deliverance You will compass me about. Selah
32.8: 'I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go; I will give counsel, My eye being upon you.'
32.9: Be you not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding; whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, that they come not near to you.
32.10: Many are the sorrows of the wicked; but he that trusts in the LORD, mercy compasses him about.
32.11: Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, you righteous; and shout for joy, all you that are upright in heart.

33.1: Rejoice in the LORD, O you righteous, praise is comely for the upright.
33.2: Give thanks to the LORD with harp, sing praises to Him with the psaltery of ten strings.
33.3: Sing to Him a new song; play skilfully amid shouts of joy.
33.4: For the word of the LORD is upright; and all His work is done in faithfulness.
33.5: He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the lovingkindness of the LORD.
33.6: By the word of the LORD were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of His mouth.
33.7: He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap; He lays up the deeps in storehouses.
33.8: Let all the earth fear the LORD; let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of Him.
33.9: For He spoke, and it was; He commanded, and it stood.
33.10: The LORD brings the counsel of the nations to nought; He makes the thoughts of the peoples to be of no effect.
33.11: The counsel of the LORD stands for ever, the thoughts of His heart to all generations.
33.12: Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD; the people whom He has chosen for His own inheritance.
33.13: The LORD looks from heaven; He beholds all the sons of men;
33.14: From the place of His habitation He looks intently upon all the inhabitants of the earth;
33.15: He that fashions the hearts of them all, that considers all their doings.
33.16: A king is not saved by the multitude of a host; a mighty man is not delivered by great strength.
33.17: A horse is a vain thing for safety; neither does it afford escape by its great strength.
33.18: Behold, the eye of the LORD is toward them that fear Him, toward them that wait for His mercy;
33.19: To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.
33.20: Our soul has waited for the LORD; He is our help and our shield.
33.21: For in Him does our heart rejoice, because we have trusted in His holy name.
33.22: Let Your mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we have waited for You.

34.1: (34-1) A Psalm of David; when he changed his demeanour before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed. (34-2) I will bless the LORD at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth.
34.2: (34-3) My soul shall glory in the LORD; the humble shall hear of it, and be glad.
34.3: (34-4) O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt His name together.
34.4: (34-5) I sought the LORD, and He answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
34.5: (34-6) They looked to Him, and were radiant; and their faces shall never be abashed.
34.6: (34-7) This poor man cried, and the LORD heard, and saved him out of all his troubles.
34.7: (34-8) The angel of the LORD encamps round about them that fear Him, and delivers them.
34.8: (34-9) O consider and see that the LORD is good; happy is the man that takes refuge in Him.
34.9: (34-10) O fear the LORD, you His holy ones; for there is no want to them that fear Him.
34.10: (34-11) The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger; but they that seek the LORD want not any good thing.
34.11: (34-12) Come, you children, hearken to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD.
34.12: (34-13) Who is the man that desires life, and loves days, that he may see good in it?
34.13: (34-14) Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking guile.
34.14: (34-15) Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
34.15: (34-16) The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous, and His ears are open to their cry.
34.16: (34-17) The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.
34.17: (34-18) They cried, and the LORD heard, and delivered them out of all their troubles.
34.18: (34-19) The LORD is nigh to them that are of a broken heart, and saves such as are of a contrite spirit.
34.19: (34-20) Many are the ills of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him out of them all.
34.20: (34-21) He keeps all his bones; not one of them is broken.
34.21: (34-22) Evil shall kill the wicked; and they that hate the righteous shall be held guilty.
34.22: (34-23) The LORD redeems the soul of His servants; and none of them that take refuge in Him shall be desolate.

35.1: A Psalm of David. Strive, O LORD, with them that strive with me; fight against them that fight against me.
35.2: Take hold of shield and buckler, and rise up to my help.
35.3: Draw out also the spear, and the battle-axe, against them that pursue me; say to my soul: 'I am Your salvation.'
35.4: Let them be ashamed and brought to confusion that seek after my soul; let them be turned back and be abashed that devise my hurt.
35.5: Let them be as chaff before the wind, the angel of the LORD thrusting them.
35.6: Let their way be dark and slippery, the angel of the LORD pursuing them.
35.7: For without cause have they hid for me the pit, even their net, without cause have they digged for my soul.
35.8: Let destruction come upon him unawares; and let his net that he has hid catch himself; with destruction let him fall in it.
35.9: And my soul shall be joyful in the LORD; it shall rejoice in His salvation.
35.10: All my bones shall say: 'LORD, who is like to You, who delivers the poor from him that is too strong for him, yes, the poor and the needy from him that spoils him?'
35.11: Unrighteous witnesses rise up; they ask me of things that I know not.
35.12: They repay me evil for good; bereavement is come to my soul.
35.13: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth, I afflicted my soul with fasting; and my prayer, may it return into my own bosom.
35.14: I went about as though it had been my friend or my brother; I bowed down mournful, as one that mourns for his mother.
35.15: But when I halt they rejoice, and gather themselves together; the abjects gather themselves together against me, and those whom I know not; they tear me, and cease not;
35.16: With the profane mockeries of backbiting they gnash at me with their teeth.
35.17: Lord, how long will You look on? Rescue my soul from their destructions, my only one from the lions.
35.18: I will give You thanks in the great congregation; I will praise You among a numerous people.
35.19: Let not them that are wrongfully my enemies rejoice over me; neither let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause.
35.20: For they speak not peace; but they devise deceitful matters against them that are quiet in the land.
35.21: Yes, they open their mouth wide against me; they say: 'Aha, aha, our eye has seen it.'
35.22: You have seen, O LORD; keep not silence; O Lord, be not far from me.
35.23: Rouse You, and awake to my judgment, even to my cause, my God and my Lord.
35.24: Judge me, O LORD my God, according to Your righteousness; and let them not rejoice over me.
35.25: Let them not say in their heart: 'Aha, we have our desire'; let them not say: 'We have swallowed him up.'
35.26: Let them be ashamed and abashed together that rejoice at my hurt; let them be clothed with shame and confusion that magnify themselves against me.
35.27: Let them shout for joy, and be glad, that delight in my righteousness; yes, let them say continually: 'Magnified be the LORD, who delights in the peace of His servant.'
35.28: And my tongue shall speak of Your righteousness, and of Your praise all the day.

36.1: (36-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David the servant of the LORD. (36-2) Transgression speaks to the wicked, methinks — there is no fear of God before his eyes.
36.2: (36-3) For it flatters him in his eyes, until his iniquity be found, and he be hated.
36.3: (36-4) The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit; he has left off to be wise, to do good.
36.4: (36-5) He devises iniquity upon his bed; he sets himself in a way that is not good; he abhors not evil.
36.5: (36-6) Your lovingkindness, O LORD, is in the heavens; Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
36.6: (36-7) Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Your judgments are like the great deep; man and beast You preserve, O LORD.
36.7: (36-8) How precious is Your lovingkindness, O God! and the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings.
36.8: (36-9) They are abundantly satisfied with the fatness of Your house; and You make them drink of the river of Your pleasures.
36.9: (36-10) For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light do we see light.
36.10: (36-11) O continue Your lovingkindness to them that know You; and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.
36.11: (36-12) Let not the foot of pride overtake me, and let not the hand of the wicked drive me away.
36.12: (36-13) There are the workers of iniquity fallen; they are thrust down, and are not able to rise.

37.1: A Psalm of David. Fret not yourself because of evil-doers, neither be you envious against them that work unrighteousness.
37.2: For they shall soon wither like the grass, and fade as the green herb.
37.3: Trust in the LORD, and do good; dwell in the land, and cherish faithfulness.
37.4: So will you delight yourself in the LORD; and He shall give you the petitions of your heart.
37.5: Commit your way to the LORD; trust also in Him, and He will bring it to pass.
37.6: And He will make your righteousness to go forth as the light, and your right as the noonday.
37.7: Resign yourself to the LORD, and wait patiently for Him; fret not yourself because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who brings wicked devices to pass.
37.8: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath; fret not yourself, it tends only to evil-doing.
37.9: For evil-doers shall be cut off; but those that wait for the LORD, they shall inherit the land.
37.10: And yet a little while, and the wicked is no more; yes, you shall look well at his place, and he is not.
37.11: But the humble shall inherit the land, and delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
37.12: The wicked plots against the righteous, and gnashes at him with his teeth.
37.13: The Lord does laugh at him; for He sees that his day is coming.
37.14: The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow; to cast down the poor and needy, to slay such as are upright in the way;
37.15: Their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bows shall be broken.
37.16: Better is a little that the righteous has than the abundance of many wicked.
37.17: For the arms of the wicked shall be broken; but the LORD upholds the righteous.
37.18: The LORD knows the days of them that are wholehearted; and their inheritance shall be for ever.
37.19: They shall not be ashamed in the time of evil; and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.
37.20: For the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the LORD shall be as the fat of lambs — they shall pass away in smoke, they shall pass away.
37.21: The wicked borrows, and pays not; but the righteous deals graciously, and gives.
37.22: For such as are blessed of Him shall inherit the land; and they that are cursed of Him shall be cut off.
37.23: It is of the LORD that a man's goings are established; and He delighted in his way.
37.24: Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down; for the LORD upholds his hand.
37.25: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
37.26: All the day long he deals graciously, and lends; and his seed is blessed.
37.27: Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore.
37.28: For the LORD loves justice, and forsakes not His saints; they are preserved for ever; but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off.
37.29: The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell in it for ever.
37.30: The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.
37.31: The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps slide.
37.32: The wicked watches the righteous, and seeks to slay him.
37.33: The LORD will not leave him in his hand, nor suffer him to be condemned when he is judged.
37.34: Wait for the LORD, and keep His way, and He will exalt you to inherit the land; when the wicked are cut off, you shall see it.
37.35: I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a leafy tree in its native soil.
37.36: But one passed by, and, indeed, he was not; yes, I sought him, but he could not be found.
37.37: Mark the man of integrity, and behold the upright; for there is a future for the man of peace.
37.38: But transgressors shall be destroyed together; the future of the wicked shall be cut off.
37.39: But the salvation of the righteous is of the LORD; He is their stronghold in the time of trouble.
37.40: And the LORD helps them, and delivers them; He delivers them from the wicked, and saves them, because they have taken refuge in Him.

38.1: (38-1) A Psalm of David, to make memorial. (38-2) O LORD, rebuke me not in Your anger; neither chasten me in Your wrath.
38.2: (38-3) For Your arrows are gone deep into me, and Your hand is come down upon me.
38.3: (38-4) There is no soundness in my flesh because of Your indignation; neither is there any health in my bones because of my sin.
38.4: (38-5) For my iniquities are gone over my head; as a heavy burden they are too heavy for me.
38.5: (38-6) My wounds are noisome, they fester, because of my foolishness.
38.6: (38-7) I am bent and bowed down greatly; I go mourning all the day.
38.7: (38-8) For my loins are filled with burning; and there is no soundness in my flesh.
38.8: (38-9) I am benumbed and sore crushed; I groan by reason of the moaning of my heart.
38.9: (38-10) Lord, all my desire is before You; and my sighing is not hid from You.
38.10: (38-11) My heart flutters, my strength fails me; as for the light of my eyes, it also is gone from me.
38.11: (38-12) My friends and my companions stand aloof from my plague; and my kinsmen stand afar off.
38.12: (38-13) They also that seek after my life lay snares for me; and they that seek my hurt speak crafty devices, and utter deceits all the day.
38.13: (38-14) But I am as a deaf man, I hear not; and I am as a dumb man that opens not his mouth.
38.14: (38-15) Yes, I am become as a man that hears not, and in whose mouth are no arguments.
38.15: (38-16) For in You, O LORD, do I hope; You will answer, O Lord my God.
38.16: (38-17) For I said: 'Lest they rejoice over me; when my foot slips, they magnify themselves against me.'
38.17: (38-18) For I am ready to halt, and my pain is continually before me.
38.18: (38-19) For I do declare my iniquity; I am full of care because of my sin.
38.19: (38-20) But my enemies are strong in health; and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.
38.20: (38-21) They also that repay evil for good are adversaries to me, because I follow the thing that is good.
38.21: (38-22) Forsake me not, O LORD; O my God, be not far from me.
38.22: (38-23) Make haste to help me, O LORD, my salvation.

39.1: (39-1) For the Leader, for Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. (39-2) I said: 'I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue; I will keep a curb upon my mouth, while the wicked is before me.'
39.2: (39-3) I was dumb with silence; I held my peace, had no comfort; and my pain was held in check.
39.3: (39-4) My heart waxed hot within me; while I was musing, the fire kindled; then spoke I with my tongue:
39.4: (39-5) 'LORD, make me to know my end, and the measure of my days, what it is; let me know how short-lived I am.
39.5: (39-6) Behold, You have made my days as hand-breadths; and my age is as nothing before You; surely every man at his best estate is altogether vanity. Selah
39.6: (39-7) Surely man walks as a mere semblance; surely for vanity they are in turmoil; he heaps up riches, and knows not who shall gather them.
39.7: (39-8) And now, Lord, what wait I for? My hope, it is in You.
39.8: (39-9) Deliver me from all my transgressions; make me not the reproach of the base.
39.9: (39-10) I am dumb, I open not my mouth; because You have done it.
39.10: (39-11) Remove Your stroke from off me; I am consumed by the blow of Your hand.
39.11: (39-12) With rebukes do You chasten man for iniquity, and like a moth You make his beauty to consume away; surely every man is vanity. Selah
39.12: (39-13) Hear my prayer, O LORD, and give ear to my cry; keep not silence at my tears; for I am a stranger with You, a sojourner, as all my fathers were.
39.13: (39-14) Look away from me, that I may take comfort, before I go hence, and be no more.'

40.1: (40-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (40-2) I waited patiently for the LORD; and He inclined to me, and heard my cry.
40.2: (40-3) He brought me up also out of the tumultuous pit, out of the miry clay; and He set my feet upon a rock, He established my goings.
40.3: (40-4) And He has put a new song in my mouth, even praise to our God; many shall see, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD.
40.4: (40-5) Happy is the man that has made the LORD his trust, and has not turned to the arrogant, nor to such as fall away treacherously.
40.5: (40-6) Many things have You done, O LORD my God, even Your wonderful works, and Your thoughts toward us; there is none to be compared to You! If I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be told.
40.6: (40-7) Sacrifice and meal-offering You have no delight in; my ears have You opened; burnt-offering and sin-offering have You not required.
40.7: (40-8) Then said I: 'Indeed, I am come with the roll of a book which is prescribed for me;
40.8: (40-9) I delight to do Your will, O my God; yes, Your law is in my inmost parts.'
40.9: (40-10) I have preached righteousness in the great congregation, indeed, I did not refrain my lips; O LORD, You know.
40.10: (40-11) I have not hid Your righteousness within my heart; I have declared Your faithfulness and Your salvation; I have not concealed Your mercy and Your truth from the great congregation.
40.11: (40-12) You, O LORD, will not withhold Your compassions from me; let Your mercy and Your truth continually preserve me.
40.12: (40-13) For innumerable evils have compassed me about, my iniquities have overtaken me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed me.
40.13: (40-14) Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; O LORD, make haste to help me.
40.14: (40-15) Let them be ashamed and abashed together that seek after my soul to sweep it away; let them be turned backward and brought to confusion that delight in my hurt.
40.15: (40-16) Let them be appalled by reason of their shame that say to me: 'Aha, aha.'
40.16: (40-17) Let all those that seek You rejoice and be glad in You; let such as love Your salvation say continually: 'The LORD be magnified.'
40.17: (40-18) But, as for me, that am poor and needy, the Lord will account it to me; You are my help and my deliverer; O my God, tarry not.

41.1: (41-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (41-2) Happy is he that considers the poor; the LORD will deliver him in the day of evil.
41.2: (41-3) The LORD preserve him, and keep him alive, let him be called happy in the land; and deliver not You him to the greed of his enemies.
41.3: (41-4) The LORD support him upon the bed of illness; may You turn all his lying down in his sickness.
41.4: (41-5) As for me, I said: 'O LORD, be gracious to me; heal my soul; for I have sinned against You.'
41.5: (41-6) My enemies speak evil of me: 'When shall he die, and his name perish?'
41.6: (41-7) And if one come to see me, he speaks falsehood; his heart gathers iniquity to itself; when he goes abroad, he speaks of it.
41.7: (41-8) All that hate me whisper together against me, against me do they devise my hurt:
41.8: (41-9) 'An evil thing cleaves fast to him; and now that he lies, he shall rise up no more.'
41.9: (41-10) Yes, my own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, who did eat of my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.
41.10: (41-11) But You, O LORD, be gracious to me, and raise me up, that I may requite them.
41.11: (41-12) By this I know that You delight in me, that my enemy does not triumph over me.
41.12: (41-13) And as for me, You uphold me because of my integrity, and set me before Your face for ever.
41.13: (41-14) Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting. Amen, and Amen.

42.1: BOOK II (42-1) For the Leader; Maschil of the sons of Korah. (42-2) As the hart pants after the water brooks, so pants my soul after You, O God.
42.2: (42-3) My soul thirsts for God, for the living God: 'When shall I come and appear before God?'
42.3: (42-4) My tears have been my food day and night, while they say to me all the day: 'Where is Your God?'
42.4: (42-5) These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me, how I passed on with the throng, and led them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, a multitude keeping holyday.
42.5: (42-6) Why are you cast down, O my soul? and why do you moan within me? Hope you in God; for I shall yet praise Him for the salvation of His countenance.
42.6: (42-7) O my God, my soul is cast down within me; therefore do I remember You from the land of Jordan, and the Hermons, from the hill Mizar.
42.7: (42-8) Deep calls to deep at the voice of Your cataracts; all Your waves and Your billows are gone over me.
42.8: (42-9) By day the LORD will command His lovingkindness, and in the night His song shall be with me, even a prayer to the God of my life.
42.9: (42-10) I will say to God my Rock: 'Why have You forgotten me? Why go I mourning under the oppression of the enemy?'
42.10: (42-11) As with a crushing in my bones, my adversaries taunt me; while they say to me all the day: 'Where is Your God?'
42.11: (42-12) Why are you cast down, O my soul? and why do you moan within me? Hope you in God; for I shall yet praise Him, the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

43.1: Be You my judge, O God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation; O deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man.
43.2: For You are the God of my strength; why have You cast me off? Why go I mourning under the oppression of the enemy?
43.3: O send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me; let them bring me to Your holy mountain, and to Your dwelling-places.
43.4: Then will I go to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding joy; and praise You upon the harp, O God, my God.
43.5: Why are you cast down, O my soul? and why do you moan within me? Hope you in God; for I shall yet praise Him, the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

44.1: (44-1) For the Leader; a Psalm of the sons of Korah. Maschil. (44-2) O God, we have heard with our ears, our fathers have told us; a work You did in their days, in the days of old.
44.2: (44-3) You with Your hand did drive out the nations, and did plant them in; You did break the peoples, and did spread them abroad.
44.3: (44-4) For not by their own sword did they get the land in possession, neither did their own arm save them; but Your right hand, and Your arm, and the light of Your countenance, because You were favourable to them.
44.4: (44-5) You are my King, O God; command the salvation of Jacob.
44.5: (44-6) Through You do we push down our adversaries; through Your name do we tread them under that rise up against us.
44.6: (44-7) For I trust not in my bow, neither can my sword save me.
44.7: (44-8) But You have saved us from our adversaries, and have put them to shame that hate us.
44.8: (44-9) In God have we gloried all the day, and we will give thanks to Your name for ever. Selah
44.9: (44-10) Yet You have cast off, and brought us to confusion; and go not forth with our hosts.
44.10: (44-11) You make us to turn back from the adversary; and they that hate us spoil at their will.
44.11: (44-12) You have given us like sheep to be eaten; and have scattered us among the nations.
44.12: (44-13) You sell Your people for small gain, and have not set their prices high.
44.13: (44-14) You make us a taunt to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.
44.14: (44-15) You make us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples.
44.15: (44-16) All the day is my confusion before me, and the shame of my face has covered me,
44.16: (44-17) For the voice of him that taunts and blasphemes; by reason of the enemy and the revengeful.
44.17: (44-18) All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten You, neither have we been false to Your covenant.
44.18: (44-19) Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from Your path;
44.19: (44-20) Though You have crushed us into a place of jackals, and covered us with the shadow of death.
44.20: (44-21) If we had forgotten the name of our God, or spread forth our hands to a strange god;
44.21: (44-22) Would not God search this out? For He knows the secrets of the heart.
44.22: (44-23) No, but for Your sake are we killed all the day; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.
44.23: (44-24) Awake, why sleep You, O Lord? Arouse Yourself, cast not off for ever.
44.24: (44-25) Wherefore hide You Your face, and forget our affliction and our oppression?
44.25: (44-26) For our soul is bowed down to the dust; our belly cleaves to the earth.
44.26: (44-27) Arise for our help, and redeem us for Your mercy's sake.

45.1: (45-1) For the Leader; upon Shoshannim; a Psalm of the sons of Korah. Maschil. A Song of loves. (45-2) My heart overflows with a goodly matter; I say: 'My work is concerning a king'; my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
45.2: (45-3) You are fairer than the children of men; grace is poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you for ever.
45.3: (45-4) Gird your sword upon your thigh, O mighty one, your glory and your majesty.
45.4: (45-5) And in your majesty prosper, ride on, in behalf of truth and meekness and righteousness; and let your right hand teach you tremendous things.
45.5: (45-6) Your arrows are sharp — the peoples fall under you — they sink into the heart of the king's enemies.
45.6: (45-7) Your throne given of God is for ever and ever; a sceptre of equity is the sceptre of your kingdom.
45.7: (45-8) You have loved righteousness, and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.
45.8: (45-9) Myrrh, and aloes, and cassia are all your garments; out of ivory palaces stringed instruments have made you glad.
45.9: (45-10) Kings' daughters are among your favourites; at your right hand does stand the queen in gold of Ophir.
45.10: (45-11) 'Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear; forget also your own people, and your father's house;
45.11: (45-12) So shall the king desire your beauty; for he is your lord; and do homage to him.
45.12: (45-13) And, O daughter of Tyre, the richest of the people shall entreat your favour with a gift.'
45.13: (45-14) All glorious is the king's daughter within the palace; her raiment is of chequer work inwrought with gold.
45.14: (45-15) She shall be led to the king on richly woven stuff; the virgins her companions in her train being brought to you.
45.15: (45-16) They shall be led with gladness and rejoicing; they shall enter into the king's palace.
45.16: (45-17) Instead of your fathers shall be your sons, whom you shall make princes in all the land.
45.17: (45-18) I will make your name to be remembered in all generations; therefore shall the peoples praise you for ever and ever.

46.1: (46-1) For the Leader; a Psalm of the sons of Korah; upon Alamoth. A Song. (46-2) God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
46.2: (46-3) Therefore will we not fear, though the earth do change, and though the mountains be moved into the heart of the seas;
46.3: (46-4) Though the waters of it roar and foam, though the mountains shake at the swelling of it. Selah
46.4: (46-5) There is a river, the streams of which make glad the city of God, the holiest dwelling-place of the Most High.
46.5: (46-6) God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; God shall help her, at the approach of morning.
46.6: (46-7) Nations were in tumult, kingdoms were moved; He uttered His voice, the earth melted.
46.7: (46-8) The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our high tower. Selah
46.8: (46-9) Come, behold the works of the LORD, who has made desolations in the earth.
46.9: (46-10) He makes wars to cease to the end of the earth; He breaks the bow, and cuts the spear in sunder; He burns the chariots in the fire.
46.10: (46-11) 'Let be, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.'
46.11: (46-12) The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our high tower. Selah

47.1: (47-1) For the Leader; a Psalm for the sons of Korah. (47-2) O clap your hands, all you peoples; shout to God with the voice of triumph.
47.2: (47-3) For the LORD is most high, awful; a great King over all the earth.
47.3: (47-4) He subdues peoples under us, and nations under our feet.
47.4: (47-5) He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob whom He loves. Selah
47.5: (47-6) God is gone up amid shouting, the LORD amid the sound of the horn.
47.6: (47-7) Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises.
47.7: (47-8) For God is the King of all the earth; sing you praises in a skilful song.
47.8: (47-9) God reigns over the nations; God sits upon His holy throne.
47.9: (47-10) The princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham; for to God belong the shields of the earth; He is greatly exalted.

48.1: (48-1) A Song; a Psalm of the sons of Korah. (48-2) Great is the LORD, and highly to be praised, in the city of our God, His holy mountain,
48.2: (48-3) Fair in situation, the joy of the whole earth; even mount Zion, the uttermost parts of the north, the city of the great King.
48.3: (48-4) God in her palaces has made Himself known for a stronghold.
48.4: (48-5) For, indeed, the kings assembled themselves, they came onward together.
48.5: (48-6) They saw, straightway they were amazed; they were affrighted, they hasted away.
48.6: (48-7) Trembling took hold of them there, pangs, as of a woman in travail.
48.7: (48-8) With the east wind You break the ships of Tarshish.
48.8: (48-9) As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God — God establish it for ever. Selah
48.9: (48-10) We have thought on Your lovingkindness, O God, in the midst of Your temple.
48.10: (48-11) As is Your name, O God, so is Your praise to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness.
48.11: (48-12) Let mount Zion be glad, let the daughters of Judah rejoice, because of Your judgments.
48.12: (48-13) Walk about Zion, and go round about her; count the towers of it.
48.13: (48-14) Mark you well her ramparts, traverse her palaces; that you may tell it to the generation following.
48.14: (48-15) For such is God, our God, for ever and ever; He will guide us eternally.

49.1: (49-1) For the Leader; a Psalm of the sons of Korah. (49-2) Hear this, all you peoples; give ear, all you inhabitants of the world,
49.2: (49-3) Both low and high, rich and poor together.
49.3: (49-4) My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be understanding.
49.4: (49-5) I will incline my ear to a parable; I will open my dark saying upon the harp.
49.5: (49-6) Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, when the iniquity of my supplanters compasses me about,
49.6: (49-7) Of them that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches?
49.7: (49-8) No man can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him —
49.8: (49-9) For too costly is the redemption of their soul, and must be let alone for ever —
49.9: (49-10) That he should still live alway, that he should not see the pit.
49.10: (49-11) For he sees that wise men die, the fool and the brutish together perish, and leave their wealth to others.
49.11: (49-12) Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling-places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.
49.12: (49-13) But man abides not in honour; he is like the beasts that perish.
49.13: (49-14) This is the way of them that are foolish, and of those who after them approve their sayings. Selah
49.14: (49-15) Like sheep they are appointed for the nether-world; death shall be their shepherd; and the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning; and their form shall be for the nether-world to wear away, that there be no habitation for it.
49.15: (49-16) But God will redeem my soul from the power of the nether-world; for He shall receive me. Selah
49.16: (49-17) Be not you afraid when one waxes rich, when the wealth of his house is increased;
49.17: (49-18) For when he dies he shall carry nothing away; his wealth shall not descend after him.
49.18: (49-19) Though while he lived he blessed his soul: 'Men will praise you, when you shall do well to yourself';
