49.19: (49-20) It shall go to the generation of his fathers; they shall never see the light.
49.20: (49-21) Man that is in honour understands not; he is like the beasts that perish.

50.1: A Psalm of Asaph. God, God, the LORD, has spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun to the going down of it.
50.2: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God has shined forth.
50.3: Our God comes, and does not keep silence; a fire devours before Him, and round about Him it storms mightily.
50.4: He calls to the heavens above, and to the earth, that He may judge His people:
50.5: 'Gather My saints together to Me; those that have made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.'
50.6: And the heavens declare His righteousness; for God, He is judge. Selah
50.7: 'Hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against you: God, your God, am I.
50.8: I will not reprove you for your sacrifices; and your burnt-offerings are continually before Me.
50.9: I will take no bullock out of your house, nor he-goats out of your folds.
50.10: For every beast of the forest is Mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills.
50.11: I know all the fowls of the mountains; and the wild beasts of the field are Mine.
50.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell you; for the world is Mine, and the fulness of it.
50.13: Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
50.14: Offer to God the sacrifice of thanksgiving; and pay your vows to the Most High;
50.15: And call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall honour Me.'
50.16: But to the wicked God says: 'What have you to do to declare My statutes, and that you have taken My covenant in your mouth?
50.17: Seeing you hate instruction, and cast My words behind you.
50.18: When you saw a thief, you had company with him, and with adulterers was your portion.
50.19: You have let loose your mouth for evil, and your tongue frames deceit.
50.20: You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your own mother's son.
50.21: These things have you done, and should I have kept silence? You had thought that I was altogether such a one as yourself; but I will reprove you, and set the cause before your eyes.
50.22: Now consider this, you that forget God, lest I tear in pieces, and there be none to deliver.
50.23: Whoever offers the sacrifice of thanksgiving honours Me; and to him that orders his way aright will I show the salvation of God.'

51.1: (51-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David; (51-2) When Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba. (51-3) Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your mercy; according to the multitude of Your compassions blot out my transgressions.
51.2: (51-4) Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
51.3: (51-5) For I know my transgressions; and my sin is ever before me.
51.4: (51-6) Against You, You only, have I sinned, and done that which is evil in Your sight; that You may be justified when You speak, and be in the right when You judge.
51.5: (51-7) Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me.
51.6: (51-8) Behold, You desire truth in the inward parts; make me, therefore, to know wisdom in my inmost heart.
51.7: (51-9) Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
51.8: (51-10) Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which You have crushed may rejoice.
51.9: (51-11) Hide Your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.
51.10: (51-12) Create me a clean heart, O God; and renew a stedfast spirit within me.
51.11: (51-13) Cast me not away from Your presence; and take not Your holy spirit from me.
51.12: (51-14) Restore to me the joy of Your salvation; and let a willing spirit uphold me.
51.13: (51-15) Then will I teach transgressors Your ways; and sinners shall return to You.
51.14: (51-16) Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, You God of my salvation; so shall my tongue sing aloud of Your righteousness.
51.15: (51-17) O Lord, open You my lips; and my mouth shall declare Your praise.
51.16: (51-18) For You delight not in sacrifice, else would I give it; You have no pleasure in burnt-offering.
51.17: (51-19) The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
51.18: (51-20) Do good in Your favour to Zion; build You the walls of Jerusalem.
51.19: (51-21) Then will You delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt-offering and whole offering; then will they offer bullocks upon Your altar.

52.1: (52-1) For the Leader. Maschil of David; (52-2) when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said to him: 'David is come to the house of Ahimelech.' (52-3) Why do you boast yourself of evil, O mighty man? The mercy of God endures continually.
52.2: (52-4) Your tongue devises destruction; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.
52.3: (52-5) You love evil more than good; falsehood rather than speaking righteousness. Selah
52.4: (52-6) You love all devouring words, the deceitful tongue.
52.5: (52-7) God will likewise break you for ever, He will take you up, and pluck you out of your tent, and root you out of the land of the living. Selah
52.6: (52-8) The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him:
52.7: (52-9) 'Indeed, this is the man that made not God his stronghold; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.'
52.8: (52-10) But as for me, I am like a leafy olive-tree in the house of God; I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.
52.9: (52-11) I will give You thanks for ever, because You have done it; and I will wait for Your name, for it is good, in the presence of Your saints.

53.1: (53-1) For the Leader; upon Mahalath. Maschil of David. (53-2) The fool has said in his heart: 'There is no God'; they have dealt corruptly, and have done abominable iniquity; there is none that does good.
53.2: (53-3) God looked forth from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any man of understanding, that did seek after God.
53.3: (53-4) Every one of them is unclean, they are together become impure; there is none that does good, no, not one.
53.4: (53-5) 'Shall not the workers of iniquity know it, who eat up My people as they eat bread, and call not upon God?'
53.5: (53-6) There are they in great fear, where no fear was; for God has scattered the bones of him that encamps against you; You have put them to shame, because God has rejected them.
53.6: (53-7) Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God turns the captivity of His people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

54.1: (54-1) For the Leader; with string-music. Maschil of David: (54-2) when the Ziphites came and said to Saul: 'Does not David hide himself with us?' (54-3) O God, save me by Your name, and right me by Your might.
54.2: (54-4) O God, hear my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth.
54.3: (54-5) For strangers are risen up against me, and violent men have sought after my soul; they have not set God before them. Selah
54.4: (54-6) Behold, God is my helper; the Lord is for me as the upholder of my soul.
54.5: (54-7) He will requite the evil to them that lie in wait for me; destroy You them in Your truth.
54.6: (54-8) With a freewill-offering will I sacrifice to You; I will give thanks to Your name, O LORD, for it is good.
54.7: (54-9) For He has delivered me out of all trouble; and my eye has gazed upon my enemies.

55.1: (55-1) For the Leader; with string-music. Maschil of David. (55-2) Give ear, O God, to my prayer; and hide not Yourself from my supplication.
55.2: (55-3) Attend to me, and hear me; I am distraught in my complaint, and will moan;
55.3: (55-4) Because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked; for they cast mischief upon me, and in anger they persecute me.
55.4: (55-5) My heart does writhe within me; and the terrors of death are fallen upon me.
55.5: (55-6) Fear and trembling come upon me, and horror has overwhelmed me.
55.6: (55-7) And I said: 'Oh that I had wings like a dove! then would I fly away, and be at rest.
55.7: (55-8) Indeed, then would I wander far off, I would lodge in the wilderness. Selah
55.8: (55-9) I would haste me to a shelter from the stormy wind and tempest.'
55.9: (55-10) Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongue; for I have seen violence and strife in the city.
55.10: (55-11) Day and night they go about it upon the walls of it; iniquity also and mischief are in the midst of it.
55.11: (55-12) Wickedness is in the midst of it; oppression and guile depart not from her broad place.
55.12: (55-13) For it was not an enemy that taunted me, then I could have borne it; neither was it my adversary that did magnify himself against me, then I would have hid myself from him.
55.13: (55-14) But it was you, a man my equal, my companion, and my familiar friend;
55.14: (55-15) We took sweet counsel together, in the house of God we walked with the throng.
55.15: (55-16) May He incite death against them, let them go down alive into the nether-world; for evil is in their dwelling, and within them.
55.16: (55-17) As for me, I will call upon God; and the LORD shall save me.
55.17: (55-18) Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I complain, and moan; and He has heard my voice.
55.18: (55-19) He has redeemed my soul in peace so that none came nigh me; for they were many that strove with me.
55.19: (55-20) God shall hear, and humble them, even He that is enthroned of old, Selah, such as have no changes, and fear not God.
55.20: (55-21) He has put forth his hands against them that were at peace with him; he has profaned his covenant.
55.21: (55-22) Smoother than cream were the speeches of his mouth, but his heart was war; his words were softer than oil, yet were they keen-edged swords.
55.22: (55-23) Cast your burden upon the LORD, and He will sustain you; He will never suffer the righteous to be moved.
55.23: (55-24) But You, O God, will bring them down into the nethermost pit; men of blood and deceit shall not live out half their days; but as for me, I will trust in You.

56.1: (56-1) For the Leader; upon Jonath-elem-rehokim. A Psalm of David; Michtam; when the Philistines took him in Gath. (56-2) Be gracious to me, O God, for man would swallow me up; all the day he fighting oppresses me.
56.2: (56-3) They that lie in wait for me would swallow me up all the day; for they are many that fight against me, O Most High,
56.3: (56-4) In the day that I am afraid, I will put my trust in You.
56.4: (56-5) In God — I will praise His word — in God do I trust, I will not be afraid; what can flesh do to me?
56.5: (56-6) All the day they trouble my affairs; all their thoughts are against me for evil.
56.6: (56-7) They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps; according as they have waited for my soul.
56.7: (56-8) Because of iniquity cast them out; in anger bring down the peoples, O God.
56.8: (56-9) You has counted my wanderings; put You my tears into Your bottle; are they not in Your book?
56.9: (56-10) Then shall my enemies turn back in the day that I call; this I know, that God is for me.
56.10: (56-11) In God — I will praise His word — in the LORD — I will praise His word —
56.11: (56-12) In God do I trust, I will not be afraid; what can man do to me?
56.12: (56-13) Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank-offerings to You.
56.13: (56-14) For you have delivered my soul from death; have You not delivered my feet from stumbling? that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

57.1: (57-1) For the Leader; Al-tashheth. A Psalm of David; Michtam; when he fled from Saul, in the cave. (57-2) Be gracious to me, O God, be gracious to me, for in You has my soul taken refuge; yes, in the shadow of Your wings will I take refuge, until calamities be overpast.
57.2: (57-3) I will cry to God Most high; to God that accomplishes it for me.
57.3: (57-4) He will send from heaven, and save me, when he that would swallow me up taunts; Selah; God shall send forth His mercy and His truth.
57.4: (57-5) My soul is among lions, I do lie down among them that are aflame; even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
57.5: (57-6) Be You exalted, O God, above the heavens; Your glory be above all the earth.
57.6: (57-7) They have prepared a net for my steps, my soul is bowed down; they have digged a pit before me, they are fallen into the midst of it themselves. Selah
57.7: (57-8) My heart is stedfast, O God, my heart is stedfast; I will sing, yes, I will sing praises.
57.8: (57-9) Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp; I will awake the dawn.
57.9: (57-10) I will give thanks to You, O Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to You among the nations.
57.10: (57-11) For Your mercy is great to the heavens, and Your truth to the skies.
57.11: (57-12) Be You exalted, O God, above the heavens; Your glory be above all the earth.

58.1: (58-1) For the Leader; Al-tashheth. A Psalm of David; Michtam. (58-2) Do you indeed speak as a righteous company? Do you judge with equity the sons of men?
58.2: (58-3) Yes, in heart you work wickedness; you weigh out in the earth the violence of your hands.
58.3: (58-4) The wicked are estranged from the womb; the speakers of lies go astray as soon as they are born.
58.4: (58-5) Their venom is like the venom of a serpent; they are like the deaf asp that stops her ear;
58.5: (58-6) Which hearkens not to the voice of charmers, or of the most cunning binder of spells.
58.6: (58-7) Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth; break out the cheek-teeth of the young lions, O LORD.
58.7: (58-8) Let them melt away as water that runs apace; when he aims his arrows, let them be as though they were cut off.
58.8: (58-9) Let them be as a snail which melts and passes away; like the untimely births of a woman, that have not seen the sun.
58.9: (58-10) Before your pots can feel the thorns, He will sweep it away with a whirlwind, the raw and the burning alike.
58.10: (58-11) The righteous shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance; he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.
58.11: (58-12) And men shall say: 'Truly there is a reward for the righteous; truly there is a God that judges in the earth.'

59.1: (59-1) For the Leader; Al-tashheth. A Psalm of David; Michtam; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him. (59-2) Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; set me on high from them that rise up against me.
59.2: (59-3) Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, and save me from the men of blood.
59.3: (59-4) For, indeed, they lie in wait for my soul; the impudent gather themselves together against me; not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O LORD.
59.4: (59-5) Without my fault, they run and prepare themselves; awake You to help me, and behold.
59.5: (59-6) You therefore, O LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, arouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to any iniquitous traitors. Selah
59.6: (59-7) They return at evening, they howl like a dog, and go round about the city.
59.7: (59-8) Behold, they belch out with their mouth; swords are in their lips: 'For who does hear?'
59.8: (59-9) But You, O LORD, shall laugh at them; You shall have all the nations in derision.
59.9: (59-10) Because of his strength, I will wait for You; for God is my high tower.
59.10: (59-11) The God of my mercy will come to meet me; God will let me gaze upon my adversaries.
59.11: (59-12) Slay them not, lest my people forget, make them wander to and fro by Your power, and bring them down, O Lord our shield.
59.12: (59-13) For the sin of their mouth, and the words of their lips, let them even be taken in their pride, and for cursing and lying which they speak.
59.13: (59-14) Consume them in wrath, consume them, that they be no more; and let them know that God rules in Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah
59.14: (59-15) And they return at evening, they howl like a dog, and go round about the city;
59.15: (59-16) They wander up and down to devour, and tarry all night if they have not their fill.
59.16: (59-17) But as for me, I will sing of Your strength; yes, I will sing aloud of Your mercy in the morning; for You have been my high tower, and a refuge in the day of my distress.
59.17: (59-18) O my strength, to You will I sing praises; for God is my high tower, the God of my mercy.

60.1: (60-1) For the Leader; upon Shushan Eduth; Michtam of David, to teach; (60-2) when he strove with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, and Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the Valley of Salt twelve thousand. (60-3) O God, You have cast us off, You have broken us down; You have been angry; O restore us.
60.2: (60-4) You have made the land to shake, You have cleft it; heal the breaches of it; for it totters.
60.3: (60-5) You have made Your people to see hard things; You have made us to drink the wine of staggering.
60.4: (60-6) You have given a banner to them that fear You, that it may be displayed because of the truth. Selah
60.5: (60-7) That Your beloved may be delivered, save with Your right hand, and answer me.
60.6: (60-8) God spoke in His holiness, that I would exult; that I would divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth.
60.7: (60-9) Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the defence of my head; Judah is my sceptre.
60.8: (60-10) Moab is my washpot; upon Edom do I cast my shoe; Philistia, cry aloud because of me!
60.9: (60-11) Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
60.10: (60-12) Have not You, O God, cast us off? And You go not forth, O God, with our hosts.
60.11: (60-13) Give us help against the adversary; for vain is the help of man.
60.12: (60-14) Through God we shall do valiantly; for He it is that will tread down our adversaries.

61.1: (61-1) For the Leader; with string-music. A Psalm of David. (61-2) Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
61.2: (61-3) From the end of the earth will I call to You, when my heart faints; lead me to a rock that is too high for me.
61.3: (61-4) For You have been a refuge for me, a tower of strength in the face of the enemy.
61.4: (61-5) I will dwell in Your Tent for ever; I will take refuge in the covert of Your wings. Selah
61.5: (61-6) For You, O God, have heard my vows; You have granted the heritage of those that fear Your name.
61.6: (61-7) May You add days to the king's days! May his years be as many generations!
61.7: (61-8) May he be enthroned before God for ever! Appoint mercy and truth, that they may preserve him.
61.8: (61-9) So will I sing praise to Your name for ever, that I may daily perform my vows.

62.1: (62-1) For the Leader; for Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. (62-2) Only for God does my soul wait in stillness; from Him comes my salvation.
62.2: (62-3) He only is my rock and my salvation, my high tower, I shall not be greatly moved.
62.3: (62-4) How long will you set upon a man, that you may slay him, all of you, as a leaning wall, a tottering fence?
62.4: (62-5) They only devise to thrust him down from his height, delighting in lies; they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah
62.5: (62-6) Only for God wait you in stillness, my soul; for from Him comes my hope.
62.6: (62-7) He only is my rock and my salvation, my high tower, I shall not be moved.
62.7: (62-8) Upon God rests my salvation and my glory; the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
62.8: (62-9) Trust in Him at all times, you people; pour out your heart before Him; God is a refuge for us. Selah
62.9: (62-10) Men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie; if they be laid in the balances, they are together lighter than vanity.
62.10: (62-11) Trust not in oppression, and put not vain hope in robbery; if riches increase, set not your heart on it.
62.11: (62-12) God has spoken once, twice have I heard this: that strength belongs to God;
62.12: (62-13) Also to You, O Lord, belongs mercy; for You render to every man according to his work.

63.1: (63-1) A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. (63-2) O God, You are my God, earnestly will I seek You; my soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You, in a dry and weary land, where no water is.
63.2: (63-3) So have I looked for You in the sanctuary, to see Your power and Your glory.
63.3: (63-4) For Your lovingkindness is better than life; my lips shall praise You.
63.4: (63-5) So will I bless You as long as I live; in Your name will I lift up my hands.
63.5: (63-6) My soul is satisfied as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth does praise You with joyful lips;
63.6: (63-7) When I remember You upon my couch, and meditate on You in the night-watches.
63.7: (63-8) For You have been my help, and in the shadow of Your wings do I rejoice.
63.8: (63-9) My soul cleaves to You; Your right hand holds me fast.
63.9: (63-10) But those that seek my soul, to destroy it, shall go into the nethermost parts of the earth.
63.10: (63-11) They shall be hurled to the power of the sword; they shall be a portion for foxes.
63.11: (63-12) But the king shall rejoice in God; every one that swears by Him shall glory; for the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.

64.1: (64-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David. (64-2) Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint; preserve my life from the terror of the enemy.
64.2: (64-3) Hide me from the council of evil-doers; from the tumult of the workers of iniquity;
64.3: (64-4) Who have whet their tongue like a sword, and have aimed their arrow, a poisoned word;
64.4: (64-5) That they may shoot in secret places at the blameless; suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.
64.5: (64-6) They encourage one another in an evil matter; they converse of laying snares secretly; they ask, who would see them.
64.6: (64-7) They search out iniquities, they have accomplished a diligent search; even in the inward thought of every one, and the deep heart.
64.7: (64-8) But God does shoot at them with an arrow suddenly; from there are their wounds.
64.8: (64-9) So they make their own tongue a stumbling to themselves; all that see them shake the head.
64.9: (64-10) And all men fear; and they declare the work of God, and understand His doing.
64.10: (64-11) The righteous shall be glad in the LORD, and shall take refuge in Him; and all the upright in heart shall glory.

65.1: (65-1) For the Leader. A Psalm. A Song of David. (65-2) Praise waits for You, O God, in Zion; and to You the vow is performed.
65.2: (65-3) O You that hears prayer, to You does all flesh come.
65.3: (65-4) The tale of iniquities is too heavy for me; as for our transgressions, You will pardon them.
65.4: (65-5) Happy is the man whom You choose, and bring near, that he may dwell in Your courts; may we be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, the holy place of Your temple!
65.5: (65-6) With wondrous works do You answer us in righteousness, O God of our salvation; You the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of the far distant seas;
65.6: (65-7) Who by Your strength set fast the mountains, who are girded about with might;
65.7: (65-8) Who still the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples;
65.8: (65-9) So that they that dwell in the uttermost parts stand in awe of Your signs; You make the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice.
65.9: (65-10) You have remembered the earth, and watered her, greatly enriching her, with the river of God that is full of water; You prepare them corn, for so prepare You her.
65.10: (65-11) Watering her ridges abundantly, settling down the furrows of it, You make her soft with showers; You bless the growth of it.
65.11: (65-12) You crown the year with Your goodness; and Your paths drop fatness.
65.12: (65-13) The pastures of the wilderness do drop; and the hills are girded with joy.
65.13: (65-14) The meadows are clothed with flocks; the valleys also are covered over with corn; they shout for joy, yes, they sing.

66.1: For the Leader. A Song, a Psalm. Shout to God, all the earth;
66.2: Sing praises to the glory of His name; make His praise glorious.
66.3: Say to God: 'How tremendous is Your work! Through the greatness of Your power shall Your enemies dwindle away before You.
66.4: All the earth shall worship You, and shall sing praises to You; they shall sing praises to Your name.' Selah
66.5: Come, and see the works of God; He is terrible in His doing toward the children of men.
66.6: He turned the sea into dry land; they went through the river on foot; there let us rejoice in Him!
66.7: Who rules by His might for ever; His eyes keep watch upon the nations; let not the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah
66.8: Bless our God, you peoples, and make the voice of His praise to be heard;
66.9: Who has set our soul in life, and suffered not our foot to be moved,
66.10: For You, O God, have tried us; You have refined us, as silver is refined.
66.11: You did bring us into the hold; You did lay constraint upon our loins.
66.12: You have caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water; but You did bring us out to abundance.
66.13: I will come into Your house with burnt-offerings, I will perform to You my vows,
66.14: Which my lips have uttered, and my mouth has spoken, when I was in distress.
66.15: I will offer to You burnt-offerings of fatlings, with the sweet smoke of rams; I will offer bullocks with goats. Selah
66.16: Come, and hearken, all you that fear God, and I will declare what He has done for my soul.
66.17: I cried to Him with my mouth, and He was extolled with my tongue.
66.18: If I had regarded iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not hear;
66.19: But truly God has heard; He has attended to the voice of my prayer.
66.20: Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, nor His mercy from me.

67.1: (67-1) For the Leader; with string-music. A Psalm, a Song. (67-2) God be gracious to us, and bless us; may He cause His face to shine toward us; Selah
67.2: (67-3) That Your way may be known upon earth, Your salvation among all nations.
67.3: (67-4) Let the peoples give thanks to You, O God; let the peoples give thanks to You, all of them.
67.4: (67-5) O let the nations be glad and sing for joy; for You will judge the peoples with equity, and lead the nations upon earth. Selah
67.5: (67-6) Let the peoples give thanks to You, O God; let the peoples give thanks to You, all of them.
67.6: (67-7) The earth has yielded her increase; may God, our own God, bless us.
67.7: (67-8) May God bless us; and let all the ends of the earth fear Him.

68.1: (68-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of David, a Song. (68-2) Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered; and let them that hate Him flee before Him.
68.2: (68-3) As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
68.3: (68-4) But let the righteous be glad, let them exult before God; yes, let them rejoice with gladness.
68.4: (68-5) Sing to God, sing praises to His name; extol Him that rides upon the skies, whose name is the LORD; and exult you before Him.
68.5: (68-6) A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in His holy habitation.
68.6: (68-7) God makes the solitary to dwell in a house; He brings out the prisoners into prosperity; the rebellious dwell but in a parched land.
68.7: (68-8) O God, when You went forth before Your people, when You did march through the wilderness; Selah
68.8: (68-9) The earth trembled, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God; even yon Sinai trembled at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
68.9: (68-10) A bounteous rain did You pour down, O God; when Your inheritance was weary, You did confirm it.
68.10: (68-11) Your flock settled in it; You did prepare in Your goodness for the poor, O God.
68.11: (68-12) The Lord gives the word; the women that proclaim the tidings are a great host.
68.12: (68-13) Kings of armies flee, they flee; and she that tarries at home divides the spoil.
68.13: (68-14) When you lie among the sheepfolds, the wings of the dove are covered with silver, and her pinions with the shimmer of gold.
68.14: (68-15) When the Almighty scatters kings in it, it snows in Zalmon.
68.15: (68-16) A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; a mountain of peaks is the mountain of Bashan.
68.16: (68-17) Why look you askance, you mountains of peaks, at the mountain which God has desired for His abode? Yes, the LORD will dwell in it for ever.
68.17: (68-18) The chariots of God are myriads, even thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in holiness.
68.18: (68-19) You have ascended on high, You have led captivity captive; You have received gifts among men, yes, among the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell there.
68.19: (68-20) Blessed be the Lord, day by day He bears our burden, even the God who is our salvation. Selah
68.20: (68-21) God is to us a God of deliverances; and to GOD the Lord belong the issues of death.
68.21: (68-22) Surely God will smite through the head of His enemies, the hairy scalp of him that goes about in his guiltiness.
68.22: (68-23) The Lord said: 'I will bring back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea;
68.23: (68-24) That your foot may wade through blood, that the tongue of your dogs may have its portion from your enemies.'
68.24: (68-25) They see Your goings, O God, even the goings of my God, my King, in holiness.
68.25: (68-26) The singers go before, the minstrels follow after, in the midst of damsels playing upon timbrels.
68.26: (68-27) 'Bless you God in full assemblies, even the Lord, you that are from the fountain of Israel.'
68.27: (68-28) There is Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, the princes of Judah their council, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
68.28: (68-29) Your God has commanded your strength; be strong, O God, You that have worked for us
68.29: (68-30) Out of Your temple at Jerusalem, where kings shall bring presents to You.
68.30: (68-31) Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds, the multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the peoples, every one submitting himself with pieces of silver; He has scattered the peoples that delight in war!
68.31: (68-32) Nobles shall come out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God.
68.32: (68-33) Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth; O sing praises to the Lord; Selah
68.33: (68-34) To Him that rides upon the heavens of heavens, which are of old; indeed, He utters His voice, a mighty voice.
68.34: (68-35) Ascribe you strength to God; His majesty is over Israel, and His strength is in the skies.
68.35: (68-36) Awful is God out of your holy places; the God of Israel, He gives strength and power to the people; blessed be God.

69.1: (69-1) For the Leader; upon Shoshannim. A Psalm of David. (69-2) Save me, O God; for the waters are come in even to the soul.
69.2: (69-3) I am sunk in deep mire, where there is no standing; I am come into deep waters, and the flood overwhelms me.
69.3: (69-4) I am weary of my crying; my throat is dried; my eyes fail while I wait for my God.
69.4: (69-5) They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head; they that would cut me off, being my enemies wrongfully, are many; should I restore that which I took not away?
69.5: (69-6) O God, You know my folly; and my trespasses are not hid from You.
69.6: (69-7) Let not them that wait for You be ashamed through me, O Lord GOD of hosts; let not those that seek You be brought to confusion through me, O God of Israel.
69.7: (69-8) Because for Your sake I have borne reproach; confusion has covered my face.
69.8: (69-9) I am become a stranger to my brethren, and an alien to my mother's children.
69.9: (69-10) Because zeal for Your house has eaten me up, and the reproaches of them that reproach You are fallen upon me.
69.10: (69-11) And I wept with my soul fasting, and that became to me a reproach.
69.11: (69-12) I made sackcloth also my garment, and I became a byword to them.
69.12: (69-13) They that sit in the gate talk of me; and I am the song of the drunkards.
69.13: (69-14) But as for me, let my prayer be to You, O LORD, in an acceptable time; O God, in the abundance of Your mercy, answer me with the truth of Your salvation.
69.14: (69-15) Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink; let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
69.15: (69-16) Let not the waterflood overwhelm me, neither let the deep swallow me up; and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.
69.16: (69-17) Answer me, O LORD, for Your mercy is good; according to the multitude of Your compassions turn You to me.
69.17: (69-18) And hide not Your face from Your servant; for I am in distress; answer me speedily.
69.18: (69-19) Draw nigh to my soul, and redeem it; ransom me because of my enemies.
69.19: (69-20) You know my reproach, and my shame, and my confusion; my adversaries are all before You.
69.20: (69-21) Reproach has broken my heart; and I am sore sick; and I looked for some to show compassion, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none.
69.21: (69-22) Yes, they put poison into my food; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
69.22: (69-23) Let their table before them become a snare; and when they are in peace, let it become a trap.
69.23: (69-24) Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to totter.
69.24: (69-25) Pour out Your indignation upon them, and let the fierceness of Your anger overtake them.
69.25: (69-26) Let their encampment be desolate; let none dwell in their tents.
69.26: (69-27) For they persecute him whom You have smitten; and they tell of the pain of those whom You have wounded.
69.27: (69-28) Add iniquity to their iniquity; and let them not come into Your righteousness.
69.28: (69-29) Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.
69.29: (69-30) But I am afflicted and in pain; let Your salvation, O God, set me up on high.
69.30: (69-31) I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify Him with thanksgiving.
69.31: (69-32) And it shall please the LORD better than a bullock that has horns and hoofs.
69.32: (69-33) The humble shall see it, and be glad; you that seek after God, let your heart revive.
69.33: (69-34) For the LORD hearkens to the needy, and despises not His prisoners.
69.34: (69-35) Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas, and every thing that moves in it.
69.35: (69-36) For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah; and they shall abide there, and have it in possession.
69.36: (69-37) The seed also of His servants shall inherit it; and they that love His name shall dwell in it.

70.1: For the Leader. A Psalm of David; to make memorial. O God, to deliver me, O LORD, to help me, make haste.
70.2: Let them be ashamed and abashed that seek after my soul; let them be turned backward and brought to confusion that delight in my hurt.
70.3: Let them be turned back by reason of their shame that say: 'Aha, aha.'
70.4: Let all those that seek You rejoice and be glad in You; and let such as love Your salvation say continually: 'Let God be magnified.'
70.5: But I am poor and needy; O God, make haste to me; You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, tarry not.

71.1: In You, O LORD, have I taken refuge; let me never be ashamed.
71.2: Deliver me in Your righteousness, and rescue me; incline Your ear to me, and save me.
71.3: Be You to me a sheltering rock, whereunto I may continually resort, which You have appointed to save me; for You are my rock and my fortress.
71.4: O my God, rescue me out of the hand of the wicked, out of the grasp of the unrighteous and ruthless man.
71.5: For You are my hope; O Lord GOD, my trust from my youth.
71.6: Upon You have I stayed myself from birth; You are He that took me out of my mother's womb; my praise is continually of You.
71.7: I am as a wonder to many; but You are my strong refuge.
71.8: My mouth shall be filled with Your praise, and with Your glory all the day.
71.9: Cast me not off in the time of old age; when my strength fails, forsake me not.
71.10: For my enemies speak concerning me, and they that watch for my soul take counsel together,
71.11: Saying: 'God has forsaken him; pursue and take him; for there is none to deliver.'
71.12: O God, be not far from me; O my God, make haste to help me.
71.13: Let them be ashamed and consumed that are adversaries to my soul; let them be covered with reproach and confusion that seek my hurt.
71.14: But as for me, I will hope continually, and will praise You yet more and more.
71.15: My mouth shall tell of Your righteousness, and of Your salvation all the day; for I know not the numbers of it.
71.16: I will come with Your mighty acts, O Lord GOD; I will make mention of Your righteousness, even of Your only.
71.17: O God, You have taught me from my youth; and until now do I declare Your wondrous works.
71.18: And even to old age and hoary hairs, O God, forsake me not; until I have declared Your strength to the next generation, Your might to every one that is to come.
71.19: Your righteousness also, O God, which reaches to high heaven; You who have done great things, O God, who is like to You?
71.20: You, who have made me to see many and sore troubles, will quicken me again, and bring me up again from the depths of the earth.
71.21: You will increase my greatness, and turn and comfort me.
71.22: I also will give thanks to You with the psaltery, even to Your truth, O my God; I will sing praises to You with the harp, O You Holy One of Israel.
71.23: My lips shall greatly rejoice when I sing praises to You; and my soul, which You have redeemed.
71.24: My tongue also shall tell of Your righteousness all the day; for they are ashamed, for they are abashed, that seek my hurt.

72.1: A Psalm of Solomon. Give the king Your judgments, O God, and Your righteousness to the king's son;
72.2: That he may judge Your people with righteousness, and Your poor with justice.
72.3: Let the mountains bear peace to the people, and the hills, through righteousness.
72.4: May he judge the poor of the people, and save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
72.5: They shall fear You while the sun endures, and so long as the moon, throughout all generations.
72.6: May he come down like rain upon the mown grass, as showers that water the earth.
72.7: In his days let the righteous flourish, and abundance of peace, till the moon be no more.
72.8: May he have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
72.9: Let them that dwell in the wilderness bow before him; and his enemies lick the dust.
72.10: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall render tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.
72.11: Yes, all kings shall prostrate themselves before him; all nations shall serve him.
72.12: For he will deliver the needy when he cries; the poor also, and him that has no helper.
72.13: He will have pity on the poor and needy, and the souls of the needy he will save.
72.14: He will redeem their soul from oppression and violence, and precious will their blood be in his sight;
72.15: That they may live, and that he may give them of the gold of Sheba, that they may pray for him continually, yes, bless him all the day.
72.16: May he be as a rich cornfield in the land upon the top of the mountains; may his fruit rustle like Lebanon; and may they blossom out of the city like grass of the earth.
72.17: May his name endure for ever; may his name be continued as long as the sun; may men also bless themselves by him; may all nations call him happy.
72.18: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who only does wondrous things;
72.19: And blessed be His glorious name for ever; and let the whole earth be filled with His glory. Amen, and Amen.
72.20: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.

73.1: BOOK III A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, even to such as are pure in heart.
73.2: But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.
73.3: For I was envious at the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
73.4: For there are no pangs at their death, and their body is sound.
73.5: In the trouble of man they are not; neither are they plagued like men.
73.6: Therefore pride is as a chain about their neck; violence covers them as a garment.
73.7: Their eyes stand forth from fatness; they are gone beyond the imaginations of their heart.
73.8: They scoff, and in wickedness utter oppression; they speak as if there were none on high.
73.9: They have set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth.
73.10: Therefore His people return here; and waters of fullness are drained out by them.
73.11: And they say: 'How does God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?'
73.12: Behold, such are the wicked; and they that are always at ease increase riches.
73.13: Surely in vain have I cleansed my heart, and washed my hands in innocency;
73.14: For all the day have I been plagued, and my chastisement came every morning.
73.15: If I had said: 'I will speak thus', behold, I had been faithless to the generation of Your children.
73.16: And when I pondered how I might know this, it was wearisome in my eyes;
73.17: Until I entered into the sanctuary of God, and considered their end.
73.18: Surely You set them in slippery places; You hurl them down to utter ruin.
73.19: How are they become a desolation in a moment! They are wholly consumed by terrors.
73.20: As a dream when one awakes, so, O Lord, when You arouse Yourself, You will despise their semblance.
73.21: For my heart was in a ferment, and I was pricked in my reins.
73.22: But I was brutish, and ignorant; I was as a beast before You.
73.23: Nevertheless I am continually with You; You hold my right hand.
73.24: You will guide me with Your counsel, and afterward receive me with glory.
73.25: Whom have I in heaven but You? And beside You I desire none upon earth.
73.26: My flesh and my heart fails; but God is the rock of my heart and my portion for ever.
73.27: For, indeed, they that go far from You shall perish; You do destroy all them that go astray from You.
73.28: But as for me, the nearness of God is my good; I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may tell of all Your works.

74.1: Maschil of Asaph. Why, O God, have You cast us off for ever? Why does Your anger smoke against the flock of Your pasture?
74.2: Remember Your congregation, which You have gotten of old, which You have redeemed to be the tribe of Your inheritance; and mount Zion, in which You have dwelt.
74.3: Lift up Your steps because of the perpetual ruins, even all the evil that the enemy has done in the sanctuary.
74.4: Your adversaries have roared in the midst of Your meeting-place; they have set up their own signs for signs.
74.5: It seemed as when men wield upwards axes in a thicket of trees.
74.6: And now all the carved work of it together they strike down with hatchet and hammers.
74.7: They have set Your sanctuary on fire; they have profaned the dwelling-place of Your name even to the ground.
74.8: They said in their heart: 'Let us make havoc of them altogether'; they have burned up all the meeting-places of God in the land.
74.9: We see not our signs; there is no more any prophet; neither is there among us any that knows how long.
74.10: How long, O God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme Your name for ever?
74.11: Why withdraw You Your hand, even Your right hand? Draw it out of Your bosom and consume them.
74.12: Yet God is my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
74.13: You did break the sea in pieces by Your strength; You did shatter the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters.
74.14: You did crush the heads of leviathan, You gave him to be food to the folk inhabiting the wilderness.
74.15: You did cleave fountain and brook; You dried up ever-flowing rivers.
74.16: Yours is the day, Your also the night; You have established luminary and sun.
74.17: You have set all the borders of the earth; You have made summer and winter.
74.18: Remember this, how the enemy has reproached the LORD, and how a base people have blasphemed Your name.
74.19: O deliver not the soul of Your turtle-dove to the wild beast; forget not the life of Your poor for ever.
74.20: Look upon the covenant; for the dark places of the land are full of the habitations of violence.
74.21: O let not the oppressed turn back in confusion; let the poor and needy praise Your name.
74.22: Arise, O God, plead Your own cause; remember Your reproach all the day at the hand of the base man.
74.23: Forget not the voice of Your adversaries, the tumult of those that rise up against You which ascends continually.

75.1: (75-1) For the Leader; Al-tashheth. A Psalm of Asaph, a Song. (75-2) We give thanks to You, O God, we give thanks, and Your name is near; men tell of Your wondrous works.
75.2: (75-3) 'When I take the appointed time, I Myself will judge with equity.
75.3: (75-4) When the earth and all the inhabitants of it are dissolved, I Myself establish the pillars of it.' Selah
75.4: (75-5) I say to the arrogant: 'Deal not arrogantly'; and to the wicked: 'Lift not up the horn.'
75.5: (75-6) Lift not up your horn on high; speak not insolence with a haughty neck.
75.6: (75-7) For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor yet from the wilderness, comes lifting up.
75.7: (75-8) For God is judge; He puts down one, and lifts up another.
75.8: (75-9) For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, with foaming wine, full of mixture, and He pours out of the same; surely the dregs of it, all the wicked of the earth shall drain them, and drink them.
75.9: (75-10) But as for me, I will declare for ever, I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
75.10: (75-11) All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up.

76.1: (76-1) For the Leader; with string-music. A Psalm of Asaph, a Song. (76-2) In Judah is God known; His name is great in Israel.
76.2: (76-3) In Salem also is set His tabernacle, and His dwelling-place in Zion.
76.3: (76-4) There He broke the fiery shafts of the bow; the shield, and the sword, and the battle. Selah
76.4: (76-5) Glorious are You and excellent, coming down from the mountains of prey.
76.5: (76-6) The stout-hearted are bereft of sense, they sleep their sleep; and none of the men of might have found their hands.
76.6: (76-7) At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, they are cast into a dead sleep, the riders also and the horses.
76.7: (76-8) You, even You, are terrible; and who may stand in Your sight when once You are angry?
76.8: (76-9) You did cause sentence to be heard from heaven; the earth feared, and was still,
76.9: (76-10) When God arose to judgment, to save all the humble of the earth. Selah
76.10: (76-11) Surely the wrath of man shall praise You; the residue of wrath shall You gird upon You.
76.11: (76-12) Vow, and pay to the LORD your God; let all that are round about Him bring presents to Him that is to be feared;
76.12: (76-13) He minishes the spirit of princes; He is terrible to the kings of the earth.

77.1: (77-1) For the Leader; for Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph. (77-2) I will lift up my voice to God, and cry; I will lift up my voice to God, that He may give ear to me.
77.2: (77-3) In the day of my trouble I seek the Lord; with my hand uplifted, my eye streams in the night without ceasing; my soul refuses to be comforted.
77.3: (77-4) When I think on it, O God, I must moan; when I muse on it, my spirit faints. Selah
77.4: (77-5) You hold fast the lids of my eyes; I am troubled, and cannot speak.
77.5: (77-6) I have pondered the days of old, the years of ancient times.
77.6: (77-7) In the night I will call to remembrance my song; I will commune with my own heart; and my spirit makes diligent search:
77.7: (77-8) 'Will the Lord cast off for ever? and will He be favourable no more?
77.8: (77-9) Is His mercy clean gone for ever? Is His promise come to an end for evermore?
77.9: (77-10) Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has He in anger shut up his compassions?' Selah
77.10: (77-11) And I say: 'This is my weakness, that the right hand of the Most High could change.
77.11: (77-12) I will make mention of the deeds of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.
77.12: (77-13) I will meditate also upon all Your work, and muse on Your doings.'
77.13: (77-14) O God, Your way is in holiness; who is a great god like to God?
77.14: (77-15) You are the God that do wonders; You have made known Your strength among the peoples.
77.15: (77-16) You have with Your arm redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
77.16: (77-17) The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You, they were in pain; the depths also trembled.
77.17: (77-18) The clouds flooded forth waters; the skies sent out a sound; Your arrows also went abroad.
77.18: (77-19) The voice of Your thunder was in the whirlwind; the lightnings lighted up the world; the earth trembled and shook.
77.19: (77-20) Your way was in the sea, and Your path in the great waters, and Your footsteps were not known.
77.20: (77-21) You did lead Your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.1: Maschil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my teaching; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
78.2: I will open my mouth with a parable; I will utter dark sayings concerning days of old;
78.3: That which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us,
78.4: We will not hide from their children, telling to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and His strength, and His wondrous works that He has done.
78.5: For He established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children;
78.6: That the generation to come might know them, even the children that should be born; who should arise and tell them to their children,
78.7: That they might put their confidence in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep His commandments;
78.8: And might not be as their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with God.
78.9: The children of Ephraim were as archers handling the bow, that turned back in the day of battle.
78.10: They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in His law;
78.11: And they forgot His doings, and His wondrous works that He had shown them.
78.12: Marvellous things did He in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.
78.13: He cleaved the sea, and caused them to pass through; and He made the waters to stand as a heap.
78.14: By day also He led them with a cloud, and all the night with a light of fire.
78.15: He cleaved rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink abundantly as out of the great deep.
78.16: He brought streams also out of the rock, and caused waters to run down like rivers.
78.17: Yet went they on still to sin against Him, to rebel against the Most High in the desert.
78.18: And they tried God in their heart by asking food for their craving.
78.19: Yes, they spoke against God; they said: 'Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
78.20: Behold, He smote the rock, that waters gushed out, and streams overflowed; can He give bread also? or will He provide flesh for His people?'
78.21: Therefore the LORD heard, and was wroth; and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger also went up against Israel;
78.22: Because they believed not in God, and trusted not in His salvation.
78.23: And He commanded the skies above, and opened the doors of heaven;
78.24: And He caused manna to rain upon them for food, and gave them of the corn of heaven.
78.25: Man did eat the bread of the mighty; He sent them provisions to the full.
78.26: He caused the east wind to set forth in heaven; and by His power He brought on the south wind.
78.27: He caused flesh also to rain upon them as the dust, and winged fowl as the sand of the seas;
78.28: And He let it fall in the midst of their camp, round about their dwellings.
78.29: So they did eat, and were well filled; and He gave them that which they craved.
78.30: They were not estranged from their craving, their food was yet in their mouths,
78.31: When the anger of God went up against them, and slew of the lusties among them, and smote down the young men of Israel.
78.32: For all this they sinned still, and believed not in His wondrous works.
78.33: Therefore He ended their days as a breath, and their years in terror.
78.34: When He slew them, then they would inquire after Him, and turn back and seek God earnestly.
78.35: And they remembered that God was their Rock, and the Most High God their redeemer.
78.36: But they beguiled Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue.
78.37: For their heart was not stedfast with Him, neither were they faithful in His covenant.
78.38: But He, being full of compassion, forgives iniquity, and destroys not; yes, many a time does He turn His anger away, and does not stir up all His wrath.
78.39: So He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes away, and comes not again.
78.40: How oft did they rebel against Him in the wilderness, and grieve Him in the desert!
78.41: And still again they tried God, and set bounds to the Holy One of Israel.
78.42: They remembered not His hand, nor the day when He redeemed them from the adversary.
78.43: How He set His signs in Egypt, and His wonders in the field of Zoan;
78.44: And turned their rivers into blood, so that they could not drink their streams.
78.45: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them; and frogs, which destroyed them.
78.46: He gave also their increase to the caterpillar, and their labour to the locust.
78.47: He destroyed their vines with hail, and their sycamore-trees with frost.
78.48: He gave over their cattle also to the hail, and their flocks to fiery bolts.
78.49: He sent forth upon them the fierceness of His anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, a sending of messengers of evil.
78.50: He levelled a path for His anger; He spared not their soul from death, but gave their life over to the pestilence;
78.51: And smote all the first-born in Egypt, the first-fruits of their strength in the tents of Ham;
78.52: But He made His own people to go forth like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
78.53: And He led them safely, and they feared not; but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
78.54: And He brought them to His holy border, to the mountain, which His right hand had gotten.
78.55: He drove out the nations also before them, and allotted them for an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
78.56: Yet they tried and provoked God, the Most High, and kept not His testimonies;
78.57: But turned back, and dealt treacherously like their fathers; they were turned aside like a deceitful bow.
78.58: For they provoked Him with their high places, and moved Him to jealousy with their graven images.
78.59: God heard, and was wroth, and He greatly abhorred Israel;
78.60: And He forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent which He had made to dwell among men;
78.61: And delivered His strength into captivity, and His glory into the adversary's hand.
78.62: He gave His people over also to the sword; and was wroth with His inheritance.
78.63: Fire devoured their young men; and their virgins had no marriage-song.
78.64: Their priests fell by the sword; and their widows made no lamentation.
78.65: Then the Lord awaked as one asleep, like a mighty man recovering from wine.
78.66: And He smote His adversaries backward; He put upon them a perpetual reproach.
78.67: Moreover He abhorred the tent of Joseph, and chose not the tribe of Ephraim;
78.68: But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which He loved.
78.69: And He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth which He has founded for ever.
78.70: He chose David also His servant, and took him from the sheepfolds;
78.71: From following the ewes that give suck He brought him, to be shepherd over Jacob His people, and Israel His inheritance.
78.72: So he shepherded them according to the integrity of his heart; and lead them by the skilfulness of his hands.

79.1: A Psalm of Asaph. O God, the heathen are come into Your inheritance; they have defiled Your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem into heaps.
79.2: They have given the dead bodies of Your servants to be food to the fowls of the heaven, the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the earth.
79.3: They have shed their blood like water round about Jerusalem, with none to bury them.
79.4: We are become a taunt to our neighbours, a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.
79.5: How long, O LORD, will You be angry for ever? How long will Your jealousy burn like fire?
79.6: Pour out Your wrath upon the nations that know You not, and upon the kingdoms that call not upon Your name.
79.7: For they have devoured Jacob, and laid waste his habitation.
79.8: Remember not against us the iniquities of our forefathers; let Your compassions speedily come to meet us; for we are brought very low.
79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the sake of the glory of Your name; and deliver us, and forgive our sins, for Your name's sake.
79.10: Wherefore should the nations say: 'Where is their God?' Let the avenging of Your servants' blood that is shed be made known among the nations in our sight.
79.11: Let the groaning of the prisoner come before You; according to the greatness of Your power set free those that are appointed to death;
79.12: And render to our neighbours sevenfold into their bosom their reproach, with which they have reproached You, O Lord.
79.13: So we that are Your people and the flock of Your pasture will give You thanks for ever; we will tell of Your praise to all generations.

80.1: (80-1) For the Leader; upon Shoshannim. A testimony. A Psalm of Asaph. (80-2) Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, You that leads Joseph like a flock; You that are enthroned upon the cherubim, shine forth.
80.2: (80-3) Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up Your might, and come to save us.
80.3: (80-4) O God, restore us; and cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved.
80.4: (80-5) O LORD God of hosts, how long will You be angry against the prayer of Your people?
80.5: (80-6) You have fed them with the bread of tears, and given them tears to drink in large measure.
80.6: (80-7) You make us a strife to our neighbours; and our enemies mock as they please.
80.7: (80-8) O God of hosts, restore us; and cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved.
80.8: (80-9) You did pluck up a vine out of Egypt; You did drive out the nations, and did plant it.
80.9: (80-10) You did clear a place before it, and it took deep root, and filled the land.
80.10: (80-11) The mountains were covered with the shadow of it, and the mighty cedars with the boughs of it.
80.11: (80-12) She sent out her branches to the sea, and her shoots to the River.
80.12: (80-13) Why have You broken down her fences, so that all they that pass by the way do pluck her?
80.13: (80-14) The boar out of the wood does ravage it, that which moves in the field feeds on it.
80.14: (80-15) O God of hosts, return, we beseech You; look from heaven, and behold, and be mindful of this vine,
80.15: (80-16) And of the stock which Your right hand has planted, and the branch that You made strong for Yourself.
80.16: (80-17) It is burned with fire, it is cut down; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.
80.17: (80-18) Let Your hand be upon the man of Your right hand, upon the son of man whom You made strong for Yourself.
80.18: (80-19) So shall we not turn back from You; quicken You us, and we will call upon Your name.
80.19: (80-20) O LORD God of hosts, restore us; cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved.

81.1: For the Leader; upon the Gittith. A Psalm of Asaph. (81-2) Sing aloud to God our strength; shout to the God of Jacob.
81.2: (81-3) Take up the melody, and sound the timbrel, the sweet harp with the psaltery.
81.3: (81-4) Blow the horn at the new moon, at the full moon for our feast-day.
81.4: (81-5) For it is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
81.5: (81-6) He appointed it in Joseph for a testimony, when He went forth against the land of Egypt. The speech of one that I knew not did I hear:
81.6: (81-7) 'I removed his shoulder from the burden; His hands were freed from the basket.
81.7: (81-8) You did call in trouble, and I rescued you; I answered you in the secret place of thunder; I proved you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
81.8: (81-9) Hear, O My people, and I will admonish you: O Israel, if you would hearken to Me!
81.9: (81-10) There shall no strange god be in you; neither will you worship any foreign god.
81.10: (81-11) I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt; open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
81.11: (81-12) But My people hearkened not to My voice; and Israel would none of Me.
81.12: (81-13) So I let them go after the stubbornness of their heart, that they might walk in their own counsels.
81.13: (81-14) Oh that My people would hearken to Me, that Israel would walk in My ways!
81.14: (81-15) I would soon subdue their enemies, and turn My hand against their adversaries.
81.15: (81-16) The haters of the LORD should dwindle away before Him; and their punishment should endure for ever.
81.16: (81-17) They should also be fed with the fat of wheat; and with honey out of the rock would I satisfy you.'

82.1: A Psalm of Asaph. God stands in the congregation of God; in the midst of the judges He judges:
82.2: 'How long will you judge unjustly, and respect the persons of the wicked? Selah
82.3: Judge the poor and fatherless; do justice to the afflicted and destitute.
82.4: Rescue the poor and needy; deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.
82.5: They know not, neither do they understand; they go about in darkness; all the foundations of the earth are moved.
82.6: I said: You are godlike beings, and all of you sons of the Most High.
82.7: Nevertheless you shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.'
82.8: Arise, O God, judge the earth; for You shall possess all nations.

83.1: (83-1) A Song, a Psalm of Asaph. (83-2) O God, keep not You silence; hold not Your peace, and be not still, O God.
83.2: (83-3) For, indeed, Your enemies are in an uproar; and they that hate You have lifted up the head.
83.3: (83-4) They hold crafty converse against Your people, and take counsel against Your treasured ones.
83.4: (83-5) They have said: 'Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.'
83.5: (83-6) For they have consulted together with one consent; against You do they make a covenant;
83.6: (83-7) The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites; Moab, and the Hagrites;
83.7: (83-8) Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre;
83.8: (83-9) Assyria also is joined with them; they have been an arm to the children of Lot. Selah
83.9: (83-10) Do You to them as to Midian; as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook Kishon;
83.10: (83-11) Who were destroyed at En-dor; they became as dung for the earth.
83.11: (83-12) Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and like Zebah and Zalmunna all their princes;
83.12: (83-13) Who said: 'Let us take to ourselves in possession the habitations of God.'
83.13: (83-14) O my God, make them like the whirling dust; as stubble before the wind.
83.14: (83-15) As the fire that burns the forest, and as the flame that sets the mountains ablaze;
83.15: (83-16) So pursue them with Your tempest, and affright them with Your storm.
83.16: (83-17) Fill their faces with shame; that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
83.17: (83-18) Let them be ashamed and affrighted for ever; yes, let them be abashed and perish;
83.18: (83-19) That they may know that it is You alone whose name is the LORD, the Most High over all the earth.

84.1: (84-1) For the Leader; upon the Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. (84-2) How lovely are Your tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!
84.2: (84-3) My soul yearns, yes, even pines for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.
84.3: (84-4) Yes, the sparrow has found a house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young; Your altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God — .
84.4: (84-5) Happy are they that dwell in Your house, they are ever praising You. Selah
84.5: (84-6) Happy is the man whose strength is in You; in whose heart are the highways.
84.6: (84-7) Passing through the valley of Baca they make it a place of springs; yes, the early rain clothes it with blessings.
84.7: (84-8) They go from strength to strength, every one of them appears before God in Zion.
84.8: (84-9) O LORD God of hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah
84.9: (84-10) Behold, O God our shield, and look upon the face of Your anointed.
84.10: (84-11) For a day in Your courts is better than a thousand; I had rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
84.11: (84-12) For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; no good thing will He withhold from them that walk uprightly.
84.12: (84-13) O LORD of hosts, happy is the man that trusts in You.

85.1: (85-1) For the Leader. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. (85-2) LORD, You have been favourable to Your land, You have turned the captivity of Jacob.
85.2: (85-3) You have forgiven the iniquity of Your people, You have pardoned all their sin. Selah
85.3: (85-4) You have withdrawn all Your wrath; You have turned from the fierceness of Your anger.
85.4: (85-5) Restore us, O God of our salvation, and cause Your indignation toward us to cease.
85.5: (85-6) Will You be angry with us for ever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?
85.6: (85-7) Will You not quicken us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?
85.7: (85-8) Show us Your mercy, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation.
85.8: (85-9) I will hear what God the LORD will speak; for He will speak peace to His people, and to His saints; but let them not turn back to folly.
85.9: (85-10) Surely His salvation is nigh them that fear Him; that glory may dwell in our land.
85.10: (85-11) Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
85.11: (85-12) Truth springs out of the earth; and righteousness has looked down from heaven.
85.12: (85-13) Yes, the LORD will give that which is good; and our land shall yield her produce.
85.13: (85-14) Righteousness shall go before Him, and shall make His footsteps a way.

86.1: A Prayer of David. Incline Your ear, O LORD, and answer me; for I am poor and needy.
86.2: Keep my soul, for I am godly; O You my God, save Your servant that trusts in You.
86.3: Be gracious to me, O Lord; for to You do I cry all the day.
86.4: Rejoice the soul of Your servant; for to You, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.
86.5: For You, Lord, are good, and ready to pardon, and plenteous in mercy to all them that call upon You.
86.6: Give ear, O LORD, to my prayer; and attend to the voice of my supplications.
86.7: In the day of my trouble I call upon You; for You will answer me.
86.8: There is none like to You among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Yours.
86.9: All nations whom You have made shall come and prostrate themselves before You, O Lord; and they shall glorify Your name.
86.10: For You are great, and do wondrous things; You are God alone.
86.11: Teach me, O LORD, Your way, that I may walk in Your truth; make one my heart to fear Your name.
86.12: I will thank You, O Lord my God, with my whole heart; and I will glorify Your name for evermore.
86.13: For great is Your mercy toward me; and You have delivered my soul from the lowest nether-world.
86.14: O God, the proud are risen up against me, and the company of violent men have sought after my soul, and have not set You before them.
86.15: But You, O Lord, are a God full of compassion and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy and truth.
86.16: O turn to me, and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid.
86.17: Work in my behalf a sign for good; that they that hate me may see it, and be put to shame, because You, LORD, have helped me, and comforted me.

87.1: A Psalm of the sons of Korah; a Song. His foundation is in the holy mountains.
87.2: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
87.3: Glorious things are spoken of You, O city of God. Selah
87.4: 'I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon as among them that know Me; behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia; this one was born there.'
87.5: But of Zion it shall be said: 'This man and that was born in her; and the Most High Himself does establish her.'
87.6: The LORD shall count in the register of the peoples: 'This one was born there.' Selah
87.7: And whether they sing or dance, all my thoughts are in You.

88.1: (88-1) A Song, a Psalm of the sons of Korah; for the Leader; upon Mahalath Leannoth. Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite. (88-2) O LORD, God of my salvation, what time I cry in the night before You,
88.2: (88-3) Let my prayer come before You, incline Your ear to my cry.
88.3: (88-4) For my soul is sated with troubles, and my life draws nigh to the grave.
88.4: (88-5) I am counted with them that go down into the pit; I am become as a man that has no help;
88.5: (88-6) Set apart among the dead, like the slain that lie in the grave, whom You remember no more; and they are cut off from Your hand.
88.6: (88-7) You have laid me in the nethermost pit, in dark places, in the deeps.
88.7: (88-8) Your wrath lies hard upon me, and all Your waves You press down. Selah
88.8: (88-9) You have put my acquaintance far from me; You have made me an abomination to them; I am shut up, and I cannot come forth.
88.9: (88-10) My eye languishes by reason of affliction; I have called upon You, O LORD, every day, I have spread forth my hands to You.
88.10: (88-11) Will You work wonders for the dead? Or shall the shades arise and give You thanks? Selah
88.11: (88-12) Shall Your mercy be declared in the grave? or Your faithfulness in destruction?
88.12: (88-13) Shall Your wonders be known in the dark? and Your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
88.13: (88-14) But as for me, to You, O LORD, do I cry, and in the morning does my prayer come to meet You.
88.14: (88-15) LORD, why cast You off my soul? Why hide You Your face from me?
88.15: (88-16) I am afflicted and at the point of death from my youth up; I have borne Your terrors, I am distracted.
88.16: (88-17) Your fierce wrath is gone over me; Your terrors have cut me off.
88.17: (88-18) They came round about me like water all the day; they compassed me about together.
88.18: (88-19) Friend and companion have You put far from me, and my acquaintance into darkness.

89.1: (89-1) Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite. (89-2) I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever; to all generations will I make known Your faithfulness with my mouth.
89.2: (89-3) For I have said: 'For ever is mercy built; in the very heavens You do establish Your faithfulness.
89.3: (89-4) I have made a covenant with My chosen, I have sworn to David My servant:
89.4: (89-5) For ever will I establish your seed, and build up your throne to all generations.' Selah
89.5: (89-6) So shall the heavens praise Your wonders, O LORD, Your faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones.
89.6: (89-7) For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD, who among the sons of might can be likened to the LORD,
89.7: (89-8) A God dreaded in the great council of the holy ones, and feared of all them that are about Him?
89.8: (89-9) O LORD God of hosts, who is a mighty one, like to You, O LORD? And Your faithfulness is round about You.
89.9: (89-10) You rule the proud swelling of the sea; when the waves of it arise, You still them.
89.10: (89-11) You did crush Rahab, as one that is slain; You did scatter Your enemies with the arm of Your strength.
89.11: (89-12) Yours are the heavens, Your also the earth; the world and the fulness of it, You have founded them.
89.12: (89-13) The north and the south, You have created them; Tabor and Hermon rejoice in Your name.
89.13: (89-14) Yours is an arm with might; strong is Your hand, and exalted is Your right hand.
89.14: (89-15) Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; mercy and truth go before You.
89.15: (89-16) Happy is the people that know the joyful shout; they walk, O LORD, in the light of Your countenance.
89.16: (89-17) In Your name do they rejoice all the day; and through Your righteousness are they exalted.
89.17: (89-18) For You are the glory of their strength; and in Your favour our horn is exalted.
89.18: (89-19) For of the LORD is our shield; and the Holy One of Israel is our king.
89.19: (89-20) Then You spoke in vision to Your godly ones, and said: 'I have laid help upon one that is mighty; I have exalted one chosen out of the people.
89.20: (89-21) I have found David My servant; with My holy oil have I anointed him;
89.21: (89-22) With whom My hand shall be established; My arm also shall strengthen him.
89.22: (89-23) The enemy shall not exact from him; nor the son of wickedness afflict him.
89.23: (89-24) And I will beat to pieces his adversaries before him, and smite them that hate him.
89.24: (89-25) But My faithfulness and My mercy shall be with him; and through My name shall his horn be exalted.
89.25: (89-26) I will set his hand also on the sea, and his right hand on the rivers.
89.26: (89-27) He shall call to Me: You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation.
89.27: (89-28) I also will appoint him first-born, the highest of the kings of the earth.
89.28: (89-29) For ever will I keep for him My mercy, and My covenant shall stand fast with him.
89.29: (89-30) His seed also will I make to endure for ever, and his throne as the days of heaven.
89.30: (89-31) If his children forsake My law, and walk not in My ordinances;
89.31: (89-32) If they profane My statutes, and keep not My commandments;
89.32: (89-33) Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with strokes.
89.33: (89-34) But My mercy will I not break off from him, nor will I be false to My faithfulness.
89.34: (89-35) My covenant will I not profane, nor alter that which is gone out of My lips.
89.35: (89-36) Once have I sworn by My holiness: Surely I will not be false to David;
89.36: (89-37) His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun before Me.
89.37: (89-38) It shall be established for ever as the moon; and be stedfast as the witness in sky.' Selah
89.38: (89-39) But You have cast off and rejected, You have been wroth with Your anointed.
89.39: (89-40) You have abhorred the covenant of Your servant; You have profaned his crown even to the ground.
89.40: (89-41) You have broken down all his fences; You have brought his strongholds to ruin.
89.41: (89-42) All that pass by the way spoil him; he is become a taunt to his neighbours.
89.42: (89-43) You have exalted the right hand of his adversaries; You have made all his enemies to rejoice.
89.43: (89-44) Yes, You turn back the edge of his sword, and have not made him to stand in the battle.
89.44: (89-45) You have made his brightness to cease, and cast his throne down to the ground.
89.45: (89-46) The days of his youth have You shortened; You have covered him with shame. Selah
89.46: (89-47) How long, O LORD, will You hide Yourself for ever? How long shall Your wrath burn like fire?
89.47: (89-48) O remember how short my time is; for what vanity have You created all the children of men!
89.48: (89-49) What man is he that lives and shall not see death, that shall deliver his soul from the power of the grave? Selah
89.49: (89-50) Where are Your former mercies, O Lord, which You did swear to David in Your faithfulness?
89.50: (89-51) Remember, Lord, the taunt of Your servants; how I do bear in my bosom the taunt of so many peoples;
89.51: (89-52) With which Your enemies have taunted, O LORD, with which they have taunted the footsteps of Your anointed.
89.52: (89-53) Blessed be the LORD for evermore. Amen, and Amen.

90.1: BOOK IV A Prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, You have been our dwelling-place in all generations.
90.2: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever You had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, You are God.
90.3: You turn man to contrition; and say: 'Return, you children of men.'
90.4: For a thousand years in Your sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.
90.5: You carry them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep; in the morning they are like grass which grows up.
90.6: In the morning it flourishes, and grows up; in the evening it is cut down, and withers.
90.7: For we are consumed in Your anger, and by Your wrath are we hurried away.
90.8: You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your countenance.
90.9: For all our days are passed away in Your wrath; we bring our years to an end as a tale that is told.
90.10: The days of our years are threescore years and ten, or even by reason of strength fourscore years; yet is their pride but travail and vanity; for it is speedily gone, and we fly away.
90.11: Who knows the power of Your anger, and Your wrath according to the fear that is due to You?
90.12: So teach us to number our days, that we may get us a heart of wisdom.
90.13: Return, O LORD; how long? And let it repent You concerning Your servants.
90.14: O satisfy us in the morning with Your mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.
90.15: Make us glad according to the days in which You have afflicted us, according to the years in which we have seen evil.
90.16: Let Your work appear to Your servants, and Your glory upon their children.
90.17: And let the graciousness of the Lord our God be upon us; establish You also upon us the work of our hands; yes, the work of our hands establish You it.

91.1: O you that dwells in the covert of the Most High, and abide in the shadow of the Almighty;
91.2: I will say of the LORD, who is my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust,
91.3: That He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.
91.4: He will cover you with His pinions, and under His wings will you take refuge; His truth is a shield and a buckler.
91.5: You shall not be afraid of the terror by night, nor of the arrow that flies by day;
91.6: Of the pestilence that walks in darkness, nor of the destruction that wastes at noonday.
91.7: A thousand may fall at Your side, and ten thousand at Your right hand; it shall not come nigh you.
91.8: Only with your eyes will you behold, and see the recompense of the wicked.
91.9: For you have made the LORD who is my refuge, even the Most High, your habitation.
91.10: There shall no evil befall you, neither shall any plague come nigh your tent.
91.11: For He will give His angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways.
91.12: They shall bear you upon their hands, lest you dash your foot against a stone.
91.13: You shall tread upon the lion and asp; the young lion and the serpent will you trample under feet.
91.14: 'Because he has set his love upon Me, therefore will I deliver him; I will set him on high, because he has known My name.
91.15: He shall call upon Me, and I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will rescue him, and bring him to honour.
91.16: With long life will I satisfy him, and make Him to behold My salvation.'
